season.rationale:
You are detrained after July's 1130 km race, with FTP around 220 W against roughly 280 W when fit. You also have a back that injures easily, a fat-loss priority, and an honest history of keeping disciplined training going for only about 4 months.

The season is therefore shaped as a low-pressure but purposeful foundation, followed by a single disciplined arc of roughly 4.5 months peaking at PBP.

Foundation phase (October to February):
- The opening rebuild re-establishes the training habit with easy aerobic work, hiking and the beginner run and row programmes.
- Gym work is back-safe: hip-hinge technique, goblet squats, RDL progression, anti-rotation core and daily hip mobility. This targets the flexibility and back problems that cause saddle and climbing issues.
- The pole vault world championship on 7 January gets a short specific block. It uses sprints, low-volume plyometrics and careful posterior-chain loading, then a two-week taper and the meet. Easy endurance continues underneath as maintenance.
- After the meet, a winter base block uses skiing, snowshoeing, fatbike, rowing, stair machine and Z2 trainer riding with progressive strength. This gives high aerobic volume at low injury risk. It also supports a modest calorie deficit, since easy volume is the best fat-loss stimulus and threshold work is not needed yet.

Disciplined phase (March to August):
- In March, road riding returns with a pre-season block that adds sweet spot and tempo. This restores FTP toward 260+ W and builds the saddle tolerance and position changes needed for April's 200 km.
- The brevet build progresses from 200 to 300 km while adding threshold and VO2max work. Tour races fit here as quality sessions.
- The specific-endurance block completes the 400 and 600 km brevets. It adds back-to-back long days, night riding, fuelling and pacing practice, and gym work shifts to strength maintenance.
- A 3–4 week taper cuts volume while keeping some intensity, so you arrive fresh at PBP.

Fat-loss approach: the deficit is kept modest throughout and removed during the vault taper, long brevets and the PBP taper, so it does not compromise performance or recovery.

block.rationale:
Dates and focus stay the same. Last week showed good steady-HR control on the trainer at about 120-135 W and solid tolerance of hikes and rides, so the aerobic base is there. Gym capacity is still low: quads burned at 12 kg and deadlifts were skipped.

sessions.description: Full rest after Sunday's big hike. 15 min hip mobility (90/90 switches, couch stretch, hip flexor stretch, hamstring strap, cat-cow, child's pose). Optional flat walk of 20-30 min at HR under 110.

sessions.title: Gym session: back-safe strength 2
sessions.description: 8 min row warm-up, then goblet squat 3x10 at 12 kg, RDL technique (dowel 2x8, then 2x8 kg dumbbells 2x8), loaded glute bridge 3x12 with 10 kg, lat pulldown 3x10 at 45 kg, cable row 3x10 at 35 kg, Pallof press 3x10/side, planks, dead bug. Finish with 10 min stretching.

sessions.description: 5 min easy technique rowing (legs, body, arms), then 3x4 min at 20-22 spm, HR 115-130, with 1 min easy between. 3 min cool-down. Damper at 4-5. Follow with 10 min hip mobility.

week.rationale:
Last week ended with unplanned volume: two easy rides plus a 2h45 mountain hike with hard climbs. Monday is therefore full rest.

The rest of the week builds the block's habits in small, purposeful doses:
- Tuesday gym: hinge and squat progression for back safety and vault prep
- Wednesday rowing intro: the start of the beginner programme
- Thursday run/walk: tendon preparation for the sprints in the vault block
- Friday Z2 ERG ride at 145 W: aerobic base for the cycling season
- Saturday rest, so Sunday's long hike stays genuinely easy (HR under 135)

Every session stays at easy intensity. Please stick to the plan rather than adding extra sessions: unplanned load is currently the main risk to your back and to consistency. Evening nutrition habits (protein snack after work, standard plate, kitchen closed at 21:00) run all week. No forecast was supplied, and you are fine with rain and darkness.

today.rationale: You stacked three unplanned days in a row: rides on Friday and Saturday, then a big hike with hard climbs on Sunday. A full rest day lets your legs and back absorb that load. today.optionalRationale: Rest is the session. The 15 min of mobility should not be skipped: hip flexibility only changes with daily frequency.

tomorrow.title: Gym session: back-safe strength 2
tomorrow.description:
Warm-up: 8 min easy row, HR under 125, then cat-cow x10, glute bridge x10 and bird dog x6/side.

Main work (rest 60-90 s between sets):
1. Goblet squat to a box at parallel, 3x10 at 12 kg. Use a 3 s descent and keep ribs down. Stop if your back tightens.
2. RDL technique: 2x8 with a dowel along your back (head, upper back and tailbone in contact), then 2x8 with 2x8 kg dumbbells. Hips back, soft knees, stop at mid-shin or wherever your back starts to round.
3. Glute bridge 3x12 with a 2 s hold, with a 10 kg plate on the hips.
4. Lat pulldown 3x10 at 45 kg.
5. Seated cable row 3x10 at 35 kg.
6. Pallof press 3x10/side.
7. Front plank 3x30 s. Side plank 2x20 s/side.
8. Dead bug 2x8/side.

Cool-down: 10 min stretching (hip flexor, hamstring strap, 90/90, pigeon), 60 s each side.

Keep any pole vaulting light and playful afterwards, 15 min max.
alternatives: If legs are still sore from the hike: do the full upper-body and core work, and cut squats and RDL to 2 sets at the same loads
tomorrow.rationale: This is the key session of the week for your back. It grooves the hip hinge before any real loading and adds the third goblet squat set you couldn't complete last week.
tomorrow.optionalRationale: This session builds the hinge pattern and posterior-chain tolerance that protect your back on long PBP climbs and when crouching at work. It also lays the base for the vault-prep loading that starts on 23 November. Skip it, and the RDL introduction slips a week, which compresses the safe progression before vault work begins.

week.focus:
Consistency week. It includes:
- Two Z2 rides at 140-150 W.
- Two run/walks building toward 3-3.5 min jogs.
- One technique row.
- Two back-safe gym sessions progressing goblet squats and introducing RDLs.
- A 2 h weekend aerobic outing.
- Daily hip mobility.
- A full rest day on Sunday.

sessions.title: Z2 ERG ride + hip mobility
sessions.description:
Indoor ERG ride, 60 min:
- 10 min warm-up at 100-130 W.
- 45 min at 140-150 W, cadence 85-95, HR cap 145 (drop 10 W if over).
- 5 min cool-down at 100 W.

Then 10 min mobility:
- 90/90 hip switches, 2x8 per side.
- Couch stretch, 2x45 s per side.
- Hamstring strap stretch, 2x45 s per leg.
- Cat-cow, 10 reps.

sessions.title: Gym A: goblet squat progression + RDL intro
sessions.description:
Warm-up:
- 8 min easy row, HR under 130.
- Bodyweight squats, 2x10.
- Dowel hinge, 2x10.

Main work:
1. Goblet squat: 4 kg x 10, then 3x10 at 12 kg with a 3 s descent. Rest 90 s.
2. Dumbbell RDL: 3x10 at 2x8 kg to mid-shin, neutral spine.
3. Glute bridge: 3x12 at 20 kg, 2 s pause at the top.
4. Lat pulldown: 3x10 at 45 kg.
5. Pallof press: 3x10 per side.
6. Plank: 3x30 s.
7. Dead bug: 2x8 per side.

Finish with 10 min stretching (couch stretch, seated forward fold, pigeon pose), 45 s each per side. Stop anything that causes back pain.

sessions.title: Run/walk 3 min jogs + technique row
sessions.description:
Outdoor run/walk with headlamp, about 35 min:
- 5 min brisk walk.
- 5 rounds of 3 min easy jog / 1.5 min walk, HR cap 145. Jog slowly enough to talk.
- 5 min walk.

At home, 20 min rowing machine:
- Damper 3-4, 20-22 strokes per minute, HR 115-135.
- Drive sequence is legs-body-arms. Recovery is arms-body-legs.
- Every 5 min, row 1 min arms-only plus body swing as a drill.

sessions.title: Run/walk 3.5 min jogs + Z2 ride
sessions.description:
Run first, while fresh, about 25 min:
- 3 min walk.
- 4 rounds of 3.5 min easy jog / 1.5 min walk, HR cap 145.
- 2 min walk.

Then ride 45 min Z2, either indoors in ERG mode or outdoors on the power-meter bike with lights:
- 5 min warm-up at 100-130 W.
- 35 min at 145-150 W, cadence 85-95, HR cap 145.
- 5 min easy.

Finish with 5 min of couch stretch and the hamstring strap stretch.

sessions.title: Gym B: hinge, hip thrust, pull/push, carries
sessions.description:
Warm-up:
- 8 min easy row, HR under 130.
- Dowel hinge, 2x10.
- Bird dog, 2x8 per side.

Main work:
1. Goblet squat: 3x10 at 12 kg. Use 14 kg only if Tuesday's three sets felt smooth.
2. Dumbbell RDL: 3x10 at 2x8 kg. Use 2x10 kg if Tuesday's sets were pain-free with a neutral spine.
3. Bench hip thrust: 3x10 at 30 kg.
4. Seated cable row: 3x12 at 35 kg.
5. Dumbbell bench press: 3x10 at 2x12 kg.
6. Side plank: 3x20 s per side.
7. Suitcase carry: 3x20 m per side at 16 kg.

Finish with 10 min stretching.

Optional: up to 15 min of playful vault technique, with no maximal jumps.

sessions.title: Easy hike or fatbike, 2 h
sessions.description:
Choose a hike or a fatbike ride, about 2 h of moving time.
- Hike: HR 105-135. Walk steep pitches with short strides and keep stops under 5 min.
- Fatbike: HR 110-140. There is no power meter, so ride by HR and spin easy on climbs.
- Bring water and a small snack.
- Swap with Sunday if the weather is clearly better then.

Finish with 5 min hip stretches.

sessions.title: Rest + 15 min hip mobility
sessions.description:
Full rest day with no cardio. Do 15 min of mobility:
- 90/90 hip switches.
- Couch stretch.
- Pigeon pose.
- Hamstring strap stretch.
- Cat-cow.
- Toe-touch reach with soft knees.

A relaxed walk with family is fine. Swap with Saturday if Sunday's weather is better for the outing.

week.rationale:
No activities from 26 Oct to 1 Nov were recorded, so I don't know if last week's 5-hour hike happened. You also tend to add unplanned extras, like the 24 Oct ride and the big Selbu hike. That makes this a consolidation week, not a big step up.

I trimmed the original ~8.5 h layout to about 7.25 h, matching the block's ~7 h target. I also added a genuine rest day on Sunday so you start week 3 fresh. At 51 and coming back from detraining, recovery is where the adaptation actually happens.

How the week is built:
- The two gym days are Tuesday and Friday, 72 h apart, so squat and hinge loading can progress safely ahead of vault prep on 23 November.
- Run/walks are on Wednesday and Thursday. Two weekly exposures build the tendon tolerance needed for strides in week 3 and sprints in December.
- Thursday pairs the second run/walk with a shorter Z2 ride, run first while fresh. This keeps two rides and two runs without adding a seventh training day.
- Saturday holds the longer outdoor session. You are fine with darkness, rain and cold, and no forecast was given, so it can swap with Sunday if Saturday's weather is clearly worse.
- Every cardio session stays under 145 bpm, with no intervals.

Fat loss: keep the 15:30 protein snack and the after-dinner kitchen-closing routine every day. Easy volume plus those two habits is the whole strategy for now, with no calorie counting.

today.title: Z2 ERG ride + hip mobility
today.description:
Indoor trainer in ERG mode, 60 min ride, then 10 min mobility.

Ride:
- Warm-up: 10 min rising from 100 to 130 W, cadence 85-90.
- Main: 45 min at 140-150 W, cadence 85-95.
- HR cap is 145 bpm, and you should expect about 120-135. If HR goes over 145, drop 10 W and stay there.
- Keep the effort flat, with no surges and no standing sprints.
- Cool-down: 5 min at 100 W.

Mobility right after the ride, about 10 min:
- 90/90 hip switches, 2x8 per side.
- Couch stretch, 2x45 s per side.
- Supine hamstring strap stretch, 2x45 s per leg.
- Cat-cow, 10 slow reps.

Fat-loss habit for today:
- Have a protein snack around 15:30, such as skyr with fruit, so you don't arrive home starving.
- After dinner, close the kitchen with a fixed routine: tea, then brush your teeth.
alternatives: Outdoor ride on the road/gravel bike with power meter and lights: 60 min at 140-150 W on flat-to-rolling roads, HR under 145. Spin easy on climbs rather than pushing over 160 W.
If you are short on time: 40 min at 140-150 W plus the full 10 min of mobility. The mobility is the part not to drop.
today.rationale: This opens week 2 of the rebuild. No activities from 26 Oct to 1 Nov reached me, so I can't confirm that last week's 5-hour hike happened. An easy, controlled Z2 ride is therefore the safest and most useful start. Your 23 Oct ride showed HR around 120 at 115-135 W, so 140-150 W is the planned small step up. Keeping the effort flat continues the steady-pacing habit we corrected after the October spinning classes. Monday is the right day for it: low impact on the legs before tomorrow's squat and RDL session.
today.optionalRationale:
This ride does three things:
- It rebuilds the low-intensity aerobic engine and fat oxidation that your 200 km brevet in April and PBP depend on, and that you lost after July.
- It is one of only two cycling sessions this week, so skipping it halves this week's bike-specific aerobic stimulus.
- It breaks the consistency streak this block exists to build.

The mobility afterwards is the daily dose that, over months, lets your hips allow a lower, less sit-bone-loaded position on the bike.

tomorrow.title: Gym A: goblet squat progression + RDL intro
tomorrow.description:
Warm-up:
- 8 min easy row, HR under 130.
- Bodyweight squats, 2x10.
- Dowel hip-hinge drill, 2x10, with the dowel touching head, upper back and tailbone.

Main work:
1. Goblet squat: 4 kg x 10 to warm up, then 3x10 at 12 kg. Take 3 s on the way down and rest 90 s between sets. Aim to complete all three sets this time.
2. Dumbbell Romanian deadlift: 3x10 at 2x8 kg. Keep a strict neutral spine, push the hips back, and use a soft knee. Stop at mid-shin, or earlier if your back starts to round. Rest 90 s.
3. Glute bridge: 3x12 with a 20 kg bar or dumbbell on the hips, 2 s pause at the top.
4. Lat pulldown: 3x10 at 45 kg.
5. Pallof press: 3x10 per side.
6. Front plank: 3x30 s.
7. Dead bug: 2x8 per side, slow, lower back pressed into the floor.

Finish with 10 min stretching, 45 s each per side:
- Couch stretch.
- Seated forward fold with soft knees.
- Pigeon pose.

Stop any exercise that causes back pain. Pole vault play is fine if you want it, but keep it light and skip it if your legs are tired from the squats.
alternatives: If the quads burn badly again at 12 kg: do 3x10 at 10 kg and keep the RDLs, since the hinge is the priority.
If the gym is impossible: home version with goblet squat, single-leg RDL and glute bridge at 3x10 each, with dead bug and plank.
tomorrow.rationale: Gym A follows an easy aerobic day, so your legs are fresh for technique-focused loading. Squats and hinges get the most attention because they protect your back.
tomorrow.optionalRationale: This session builds the hip-hinge pattern and posterior-chain strength your back currently lacks, which is why it aches on long climbs and when you crouch. That strength also has to be in place before the vault prep block starts on 23 November, when sprints and plyometrics load the back far more. Skipping it delays the RDL introduction by a week. Light Romanian deadlift 2x10 at 20 kg with a strict hip hinge, back flat, no lumbar rounding. Lat pulldown 3x10 at 40-50 kg. Glute bridge 3x12 bodyweight, pause 2 s at top. Pallof press 3x10 per side. Dead bug 2x8 per side. Plank 3x30 s with rests. Stretching 12 min: hip flexor, hamstring, adductor and figure-four holds, 2 min each. Keep all sets short of failure.
alternatives: Replace RDL with a 3x10 hip thrust at 40 kg if the hinge feels irritating
tomorrow.rationale: This is the first full gym session of the block, carrying forward the 2026-10-22 session where 12 kg goblet squats produced quad burn. Adding the third set and light RDL in a controlled way builds posterior-chain tolerance that will later support pole vault loading, while the stretching block addresses your poor hip flexion.
tomorrow.optionalRationale: Not optional. Skipping it leaves the back-safe hip-hinge pattern and hip flexion work behind for another week, which delays the squat and RDL progression this block depends on.

season.goal: Complete the 2027 randonneur brevet series (200 km in April onward) and finish Paris-Brest-Paris in August 2027 comfortably, while building general cycling fitness and longer tour-race capability, with fat loss from 24.5% toward 15% body fat and improved hip and core mobility and strength as supporting goals.

blocks.name: Rebuild and Fat Loss Foundation
blocks.focus: Re-establish training habits with easy, low-intensity aerobic volume (indoor and outdoor cycling, walking and hiking), progressive full-body gym work with a hip-hinge and core emphasis, mobility work for hip flexion, and a steady caloric deficit toward fat loss; include the 5-hour hike on 1 November and the 200 km brevet-type long ride preparation as the block progresses.

blocks.name: Pole Vault Preparation and Winter Strength
blocks.focus: Targeted power and sprint development for the 7 January 2027 pole vault world championship: short sprints, plyometrics, vault-specific technique, progressive Romanian deadlift and squat loading with strict technique to protect the back, continued easy aerobic cycling and cross-country skiing or snowshoeing as supporting volume, and a taper into the championship.

blocks.name: Winter Aerobic Base
blocks.focus: Build aerobic volume and endurance foundation using fatbike and studded-tire rides, cross-country skiing, snowshoeing and hiking; continue progressive gym strength with a focus on hip mobility, posterior chain and core stability; introduce the rowing beginner program and running beginner program (building to a comfortable 5K); keep all intensity in zone 2 with power and heart rate targets; add a weekly indoor interval session of no more than 2 hours in ERG mode at low volume to maintain neuromuscular readiness.

blocks.name: Spring Road Transition and Brevet Build
blocks.focus: Return to outdoor road cycling as conditions allow, building long-ride durability and climbing capacity with progressive weekend distances toward the 200 km brevet; introduce structured sweet-spot and tempo intervals on the power-metered road bike, maintain 1-2 gym strength sessions with maintenance loading, and continue fat loss; complete the 200 km brevet in April as a key checkpoint.

blocks.name: Endurance Specialization for PBP Pace
blocks.focus: Maximize sustained aerobic endurance and fatigue resistance for long randonneur days: multi-hour and back-to-back long rides at target brevet pace, stacked climbing sessions, tour-race simulation efforts with power targets, nutrition and pacing practice, and periodic 300 km or longer brevet-style rides; keep strength to maintenance; maintain fat loss progress toward 15% body fat.

blocks.name: Peak and Taper for Paris-Brest-Paris
blocks.focus: Final sharpening with reduced volume and short high-quality efforts, a shake-out and taper that keeps freshness high, equipment and logistics checks, and a practiced sleep and nutrition routine for the event; complete the final peak-load long ride about two weeks out, then taper volume progressively into PBP.

season.rationale: The season starts in late October 2026 from a detrained state after a 1130 km bikepacking race in July, so the first phase is a gradual, low-stress rebuild that restores habits, hip mobility, and a sustainable aerobic base while supporting fat loss; the athlete has noted that disciplined training can only be sustained for about 4 months, so intensity is deliberately withheld until the build. A brief pole vault world championship preparation on 7 January 2027 is folded into the early winter, with a sprint and plyometric emphasis and careful posterior-chain loading given the back history, followed by a taper and return to aerobic work. The winter base block (Feb to March) builds volume with cross-country skiing and fatbike riding while road conditions are poor, then the spring build (April to mid-May) introduces structured intensity and back-to-back long rides ahead of the brevet series starting with the 200 km in April. A focused specialization block (June to July) concentrates on sustained endurance, brevet-pace efficiency, and tour-race-style efforts, followed by a short taper before Paris-Brest-Paris in August. Consistent with the athlete's preference, disciplined blocks are kept under about 4 months, with a clear recovery and retention phase after the peak so that the base carries into the next season.

block.rationale: After the July bikepacking race and a detraining period, the athlete needs habit restoration before structured load. Cycling and hiking stay in a flat, low-intensity zone (trainer 135-150 W, outdoor HR under 140-145 bpm), gym is limited to two sessions per week with conservative loads because of back history and poor hip flexion. Week 1 was adjusted after the 25 October hike ran long and the 24 October ride added unplanned volume, and the week's run/walk was kept strictly easy. Week 2 adds the third goblet squat set and light RDLs, the first outdoor dry-weather rides, and an easy run/walk to rebuild the habit, while keeping all intensity flat and excluding spinning and interval work. Volume builds gradually across five weeks, with week 5 as consolidation. Dietary guidance supports fat loss but is not a training stimulus. The 1 November 5-hour hike is treated as the key long session of the re-entry period. This block sets up the pole vault preparation that follows, and the athlete's note of the 7 January championship is respected by keeping posterior-chain loading conservative.

sessions.description: Warm-up 5 min easy bike, then hip flexor and hamstring mobility 10 min. 1) Goblet squat 12 kg, 3x10 reps, rest 90 s. 2) Romanian deadlift, light, strict hip hinge, 3x10 reps, rest 90 s. 3) Lat pulldown 40 kg, 3x10 reps. 4) Glute bridge 3x12, 2 s pause at top. 5) Pallof press 3x10 per side. 6) Plank 3x30 s. Finish with 8 min stretching: hip flexor 2x60 s per side, hamstring 2x45 s per side, 90/90 hip 2x60 s per side. Stop any set where lower back pain appears.

sessions.title: Indoor steady ride (trainer, ERG)
sessions.description: Warm-up 10 min at 100-120 W, cadence 85-95. Main block 40 min at 135-150 W steady, cadence 85-95, HR 125-140 bpm; hold power flat with no surges. Cool-down 8 min at 100 W. ERG mode allowed. Total about 58 min.

sessions.title: Rest and hip mobility
sessions.description: Rest day. 10 min hip mobility: 90/90 transitions, couch stretch 2x60 s per side, supported squat hold 2x45 s, cat-camel 2 min.

sessions.title: Gym: Full body strength (upper and core)
sessions.description: Warm-up 5 min easy bike plus 5 min mobility. 1) Goblet squat 12 kg, 3x10 reps, rest 90 s. 2) Romanian deadlift light, strict hip hinge, 3x10 reps at 10-12 kg, rest 90 s. 3) Lat pulldown 45 kg, 3x10 reps. 4) Seated cable row 40 kg, 3x10 reps. 5) Pallof press 3x10 per side. 6) Dead bug 3x8 per side. 7) Plank 3x30-40 s. Finish with 10 min stretching: hip flexor, hamstring, and 90/90 holds, 2x60 s each.

sessions.title: Outdoor road or gravel easy ride (dry conditions)
sessions.description: Outdoor ride on the road or gravel bike with power meter, 60-75 min, dry conditions only. Power 130-145 W, HR under 140 bpm. Keep a relaxed, neutral upright position; alternate hand positions every 15 min to reduce sit-bone pressure. Stop for a short stretch every 30 min. Lights if dark.

sessions.title: Easy walk on flat or rolling terrain
sessions.description: Easy walk on flat or gently rolling terrain, 40-50 min, HR under 130 bpm. Stretch 5 min afterwards.

sessions.title: Run/walk: beginner running (easy)
sessions.description: Run/walk 30 min: 4 min easy jog, 1 min walk, repeated 6 times. Heart rate strictly under 145 bpm during jogs; walk if it rises above. Keep pace conversational. Head lamp if dark. Stretch 5 min afterwards.

week.rationale: Week 1 was completed with a strong indoor ride and gym session, though the run/walk was missed. This week keeps the ramp gradual: two gym sessions with conservative loads for hip-hinge and back safety, one indoor steady ride at 135-150 W, an outdoor road or gravel ride at HR under 140 bpm, an easy run/walk to rebuild the habit, and daily hip mobility. Intervals and spinning are excluded. The 1 November 5-hour hike falls before this week, so the rest of the week keeps load light to build on it. Pole vault preparation is not started yet; the aerobic base comes first.

today.description: Warm-up 5 min easy bike, then hip flexor and hamstring mobility 10 min. 1) Goblet squat 12 kg, 3x10 reps, rest 90 s. 2) Romanian deadlift, light (bar or 10 kg dumbbells), strict hip hinge, 3x10 reps, rest 90 s. 3) Lat pulldown 40 kg, 3x10 reps. 4) Glute bridge 3x12, 2 s pause at top. 5) Pallof press 3x10 per side. 6) Plank 3x30 s. Finish with 8 min stretching: hip flexor stretch 2x60 s per side, hamstring stretch 2x45 s per side, 90/90 hip stretch 2x60 s per side. Stop any set where lower back pain appears.
alternatives: If the back feels tight on arrival, drop the RDLs to 2 sets and keep all other work
If time is short, skip the Pallof press and keep the stretching block
today.rationale: Week 1's gym sessions were completed with good technique control, and today continues the conservative, back-safe progression. Lower-body hip-hinge work at 12 kg goblet squat and light RDLs builds posterior-chain strength while the back is still re-adapting. The longer stretching block responds to the coach's note that 2.5 minutes will not move the hips.
today.optionalRationale: Not optional. Skipping this session removes the second consecutive lower-body hip-hinge stimulus that the rebuild needs to load the posterior chain safely, and it delays the hip flexion work that the athlete needs before the pole vault block and the brevet build.

tomorrow.title: Indoor steady ride (trainer, ERG)
tomorrow.description: Warm-up 10 min at 100-120 W, cadence 85-95. Main block 40 min at 135-150 W steady, cadence 85-95, HR 125-140 bpm; hold power flat with no surges. Cool-down 8 min at 100 W. ERG mode allowed. Total about 58 min.
alternatives: Outdoor road or gravel ride at 130-145 W if dry and daylight allows
tomorrow.rationale: Steady aerobic volume rebuilds the base without the fatigue of intervals. Holding power flat in the 135-150 W band builds the aerobic foundation the spring brevet build depends on, and avoids the erratic surge pattern seen on 15 October.
tomorrow.optionalRationale: Not optional. This is the main aerobic stimulus of the week, and skipping it leaves the aerobic base behind the rebuild schedule, which makes the 200 km brevet in April harder to reach comfortably.

season.rationale: The season is shaped around three fixed events and the athlete's own observation that disciplined training only holds for about four months. The first block is a short, back-safe rebuild that also carries vault-specific power work and a taper into the 7 January pole vault world championship, because that event is too close to ignore and too explosive to bolt onto a generic base block. After 7 January the plan deliberately returns to easy aerobic rebuilding through the Norwegian winter using the fatbike, cross-country skiing, snowshoeing, rowing and the gym, with strength and hip mobility as a constant thread for fat loss, back health and sit-bone comfort. A dedicated brevet-preparation block then builds the durability and fuelling needed for the April 200 km and the rest of the series, using the March return of road cycling. The long build block is the only truly disciplined, high-load phase and is timed so its peak lands at Paris-Brest-Proust in August, respecting the four-month limit on optimal training. A final taper block sharpens and freshens the athlete for the event. Intensity is introduced late and sparingly so that every session has a clear purpose, and the ordinary tour-race fitness the athlete wants is developed as a by-product of the brevet and build blocks rather than as separate racing load.

block.rationale: The block is revised to accommodate the newly confirmed pole vault world championship on 7 January 2027. The first two weeks remain a gentle aerobic and strength re-entry from a detrained state, with daily hip mobility and technique-first gym work protecting the back. From week 3 onward, easy aerobic volume is maintained but the strength work shifts toward back-safe posterior-chain loading and hip/trunk capacity, which is the foundation for vaulting. Weeks 6-8 introduce low-volume, high-quality vault-specific power — short sprints, low-level plyometrics and technical vault work — with full recovery between efforts and no aerobic intensity. Weeks 9-11 taper volume while retaining short explosive touches into 7 January, followed by immediate recovery. Fat-loss habits and hip mobility run throughout so the block supports both the vault event and the later 2027 endurance season.

week.focus: Re-entry week 1: easy aerobic consistency, technique-first gym, daily hip mobility, and arriving fresh for the 5-hour hike on 1 November.

sessions.title: Rest and hip mobility
sessions.description: Full rest day. 15–20 minutes of hip mobility and stretching: 90/90 hip switches 2x8/side, half-kneeling hip flexor stretch 2x45s/side, cat-cow 2x10, adductor rock-back 2x10/side, hamstring floss 2x10/side. Keep breathing easy; no training load.

sessions.title: Easy indoor trainer ride
sessions.description: 60 minutes on the indoor trainer in ERG mode. Warm-up 15 min at 90–110 W, then 35 min steady at 140–150 W with cadence 85–95 rpm, then 10 min easy spin. Cap HR at 145 bpm; if HR drifts more than 10 bpm above target, reduce power immediately. Flat, surge-free effort — no intervals.

sessions.title: Gym: technique-first full-body strength
sessions.description: 45–60 min at the gym. Warm-up 8 min easy rowing under 130 bpm. Goblet squat 3x10 at 12 kg (add the third set this week). Romanian deadlift 3x8 at light load (20–30 kg total) with a strict hip hinge and neutral spine — stop if the back feels loaded. Glute bridge 3x12. Lat pulldown 3x10 at 40–50 kg. Pallof press 3x10/side. Plank 3x30s. Finish with 8–10 minutes of hip and hamstring stretching.

sessions.title: Rest and hip mobility
sessions.description: Full rest day to absorb the first two sessions and protect the 5-hour hike. Optional 15–20 minutes of hip mobility and easy walking.

sessions.title: Easy indoor trainer ride
sessions.description: 50 minutes on the indoor trainer in ERG mode. Warm-up 10 min at 90–110 W, then 30 min steady at 140–150 W, cadence 85–95 rpm, then 10 min easy spin. HR under 145 bpm, flat effort line. Optional: 10 minutes of hip mobility afterwards.

sessions.title: Rest and hip mobility
sessions.description: Full rest day ahead of Sunday's 5-hour hike. 15–20 minutes of hip mobility and stretching, plus 10 minutes of easy walking if the legs feel stiff. Prioritise sleep and hydration.

sessions.title: 5-hour mountain hike
sessions.description: 5 hours of mountain hiking at easy aerobic effort, HR mostly under 135 bpm. Walk steep pitches with short strides rather than surging; cap summit stops at 5 minutes. Carry food and water for the full duration. This is the week's key session — arrive fresh and keep the effort controlled.

week.rationale: The athlete is detrained after the July bikepacking race and completed an unplanned 2h45 mountain hike on 25 October with sustained HR in the 140s–160s, plus two unplanned easy indoor rides on 23–24 October. Week 1 therefore stays deliberately light: two short easy aerobic sessions, one technique-first gym session, one short run/walk, and a full rest day before Sunday's 5-hour hike. The 5-hour hike on 1 November is the week's key session and must be protected. The 7 January pole vault world championship is now a fixed event, so this week begins the back-safe posterior-chain and hip-mobility thread that will support vault-specific work later in the block, without adding explosive load yet. All aerobic work is capped easy (RPE 3–5, HR under ~145) and there are no structured intervals.

today.title: Rest and hip mobility
today.description: Full rest day. 15–20 minutes of hip mobility and stretching: 90/90 hip switches 2x8/side, half-kneeling hip flexor stretch 2x45s/side, cat-cow 2x10, adductor rock-back 2x10/side, hamstring floss 2x10/side. Keep breathing easy; no training load.
alternatives: If you feel stiff, add 10 minutes of easy walking.
today.rationale: Rest is the best choice today: you completed an unplanned 2h45 mountain hike yesterday with sustained HR in the 140s–160s, well above the easy cap and a significant load six days before the 5-hour hike on 1 November. Your legs and back need recovery, and the hip mobility work directly supports your sit-bone comfort and back resilience goals without adding training stress.
today.optionalRationale: Rest day — no optionality assessment needed; recovery is the priority after yesterday's unplanned 2h45 hike.

tomorrow.title: Easy indoor trainer ride
tomorrow.description: 60 minutes on the indoor trainer in ERG mode. Warm-up 15 min at 90–110 W, then 35 min steady at 140–150 W with cadence 85–95 rpm, then 10 min easy spin. Cap HR at 145 bpm; if HR drifts more than 10 bpm above target, reduce power immediately. Flat, surge-free effort — no intervals.
alternatives: If legs feel heavy from Sunday's hike, reduce to 45 minutes easy spinning at 120–140 W.
tomorrow.rationale: This ride re-establishes steady aerobic work after the unplanned hike and builds the fat-oxidation base that underpins your fat-loss goal. Keeping it flat and surge-free protects your back and legs ahead of the 5-hour hike on 1 November.
tomorrow.optionalRationale: This ride builds the steady aerobic base and fat-oxidation capacity that underpins your fat-loss goal and your return to cycling fitness for the 2027 brevets. Skipping it delays the aerobic re-entry and reduces the weekly volume needed to support the 5-hour hike on 1 November.

block.rationale: The block keeps its name, dates and overall shape, but the first weeks are revised to reflect what actually happened: the athlete is more detrained than the original plan assumed, the 5-hour hike on 1 November was a large unplanned load, and the 25 October mountain hike added further fatigue. From week 3 the block builds easy aerobic volume and posterior-chain capacity as originally planned, and weeks 4-5 introduce vault movement preparation and the first careful power touches. Weeks 6-8 remain the vault-specific power build with low aerobic volume and full recovery, weeks 9-11 taper into 7 January, and the block closes with recovery. Fat-loss habits and daily hip mobility run throughout, and no aerobic intensity is added before the vault taper so that every session has a clear purpose.

week.focus: Recovery and aerobic consistency after the 5-hour hike: full rest, steady trainer work at 140-150 W, two technique-first gym sessions with third goblet squat set and light Romanian deadlifts, beginner run/walk, fatbike endurance, and rowing with daily hip mobility.

Absorb Sunday's 5-hour hike; keep the back and hips moving without loading them.

sessions.title: Easy steady indoor ride
sessions.description: Indoor trainer, ERG mode. 10 min warm-up at 90-110 W, then 40 min steady at 140-150 W, cadence 85-95, HR capped at 145 bpm; if HR drifts more than 10 bpm above target, back off rather than surge. 5 min cool-down. Flat effort line, no intervals.

sessions.title: Gym strength A: squat, hinge, pull, core
sessions.description: 10 min easy rowing warm-up at HR under 130 bpm. Goblet squat 3x10 at 12 kg, adding the third set but stopping if the quads burn sharply. Romanian deadlift 3x8 at light load (empty bar or 20-25 kg) with a strict hip hinge and neutral spine. Glute bridge 3x12. Lat pulldown 3x10 at 40-50 kg. Pallof press 3x10/side. Plank 3x30 s. Finish with 8-10 minutes of stretching for hip flexors, hamstrings and adductors.

sessions.title: Easy run/walk
sessions.description: 30 min easy run/walk: 4 min jog / 1 min walk, HR under 145 bpm, flat route. This is the beginner running progression and the session missed last week; keep it genuinely easy and stop early if the legs feel heavy from Wednesday's gym work.

sessions.title: Gym strength B: hinge emphasis and trunk
sessions.description: 10 min easy rowing warm-up at HR under 130 bpm. Goblet squat 3x10 at 12 kg. Romanian deadlift 3x8 at light load with a strict hinge. Single-leg glute bridge 3x8/side. Seated cable row or dumbbell row 3x10. Dead bug 3x8/side. Side plank 3x20 s/side. Finish with 8-10 minutes of hip and thoracic stretching.

sessions.title: Fatbike endurance ride
sessions.description: 2 h easy fatbike ride on gravel or forest roads, HR 120-140 bpm, RPE 4-5, no power target. Keep the effort flat and steady, walk any steep pitch that pushes HR above 145, and keep stops short. Studded tyres and lights as needed.

sessions.title: Easy indoor row and hip mobility
sessions.description: Indoor rowing, beginner progression: 5 min easy warm-up, then 3x8 min at easy conversational pace (HR 120-140 bpm) with 2 min easy between, 5 min cool-down. Finish with 15 minutes of hip mobility: 90/90 switches, hip flexor stretch, adductor rock-backs, cat-cow.

block.rationale: This block serves as a critical physiological and psychological reset following the detraining period after the July bikepacking race. Given the athlete's history of burnout with disciplined training beyond 4 months and specific lower back vulnerability, the primary objective is not performance gain but habit formation and tissue tolerance. We utilize low-intensity steady-state (LISS) cycling and hiking to maximize fat oxidation without triggering excessive hunger or cortisol spikes associated with high intensity. Strength work focuses exclusively on posterior chain activation and hip mobility to address the root causes of sit-bone discomfort and back ache, ensuring the body is structurally prepared for the upcoming Pole Vault preparation phase. The volume is capped to prevent injury while re-establishing neuromuscular patterns for running and rowing.

block.rationale: This block serves as a critical physiological and psychological reset following the detraining period after the July bikepacking race. Given the athlete's history of burnout with disciplined training beyond 4 months and specific lower back vulnerability, the primary objective is not performance gain but habit formation and tissue tolerance. We utilize low-intensity steady-state (LISS) cycling and hiking to maximize fat oxidation without triggering excessive hunger or cortisol spikes associated with high intensity. Strength work focuses exclusively on posterior chain activation and hip mobility to address the root causes of sit-bone discomfort and back ache, ensuring the body is structurally prepared for the upcoming Pole Vault preparation phase. The volume is capped to prevent injury while re-establishing neuromuscular patterns for running and rowing.

sessions.description: Steady aerobic spin to promote blood flow and recovery. Warm-up 10 min easy. Main set 40 min at 140-150 W, HR 125-140 bpm. Cadence 90+ rpm. Cool-down 5 min easy. Keep effort conversational. No surges.

sessions.title: Long Mountain Hike

season.rationale: The season is divided into phases that respect the athlete's training history, preferences, and realistic capacity for disciplined training. The athlete has shown he maintains disciplined training for at most 4 months, so the plan builds a broad base of aerobic fitness, strength, and fat loss through the winter using low-intensity, habit-focused work that is sustainable and enjoyable, including indoor cycling, rowing, running, hiking, and strength training. As spring approaches and outdoor road cycling becomes possible, the plan gradually shifts to more specific endurance and race-oriented training, with a focused build block leading into the 200 km brevet in April. Following the brevet, the athlete maintains fitness through a lighter maintenance period before a final specialized build for Paris-Brest-Paris in August, with a proper taper. The early emphasis on fat loss and strength is critical because the athlete's primary goal is fat loss, and his back and hip limitations require careful posterior-chain loading and mobility work to prevent injury during long rides. The training is designed to be time-efficient, with weekday sessions capped at 2 hours and longer weekend rides/hikes, and uses power targets for cycling and HR targets for other activities, while strength training is gym-based and specific. The plan avoids unnecessary volume and intensity, ensuring each workout counts, and builds in flexibility for winter conditions (cross-country skiing, snowshoeing, fatbike) to maintain aerobic fitness without resorting to road cycling in poor conditions.

today.rationale: You climbed and hiked for 5 hours on 1 November on top of a week that already included an unplanned long hike. sessions.title: Back-safe full-body strength B
sessions.description: Warm up with 5 minutes easy cardio and mobility. Complete goblet squat 3x8 at 12 kg; Romanian deadlift 2x8 at Wednesday's load only if there has been no back reaction, otherwise substitute glute bridges; glute bridge 3x12; lat pulldown 3x10-12; Pallof press 3x10 per side; dead bug 2x8 per side; and plank 2x20-30 seconds only if trunk control remains clean. Keep at least three repetitions in reserve. Finish with 10 minutes of hip and hamstring mobility, then stop rather than adding conditioning.

Do 10 minutes of gentle mobility and prepare food, fluids, clothing, and breaks for the hike.

Begin fueling within the first hour, eat regularly, drink to thirst, and keep summit and other stops purposeful at about 5 minutes where practical. Use a comfortable backpack and footwear, and finish with gentle hip mobility rather than additional training.

week.rationale: The extra 60-minute ride on 24 October and demanding 11.1 km mountain hike on 25 October make recovery the priority at the start of this week. week.focus: Recover from the long hike, then restore consistent easy aerobic training, technique-first strength, rowing skill, hip mobility, and cautious run/walk exposure.

sessions.title: Recovery and mobility
sessions.description: Full training rest after the long-hike load. Take an optional relaxed 10-20-minute walk only if it helps stiffness, but do not count it as training. Complete 10 minutes of gentle hip-flexor, hamstring, glute, and thoracic mobility without forcing end ranges. Eat a normal protein-containing dinner and prepare a planned evening snack to avoid grazing.

sessions.title: Steady indoor aerobic ride
sessions.description: Use the trainer in ERG mode if legs are adequately recovered. Warm up for 10 minutes at 90-120 W, ride 45 minutes steadily at 140-150 W with cadence 85-95 rpm, then cool down for 10 minutes at 90-110 W. Keep HR approximately 125-145 bpm and avoid surges; reduce power if HR drifts above this range. Finish with 8-10 minutes of hip-flexor and hamstring mobility. If hike soreness is substantial, replace the ride with 25-30 minutes of very easy walking rather than postponing it.

sessions.title: Gym strength and beginner rowing
sessions.description: Begin with 20 minutes of easy rowing below HR 130: 5 minutes of relaxed technique, then 10 x 1 minute at controlled pressure with 30 seconds very easy between, focusing on legs-body-arms sequencing and a long, unforced recovery. After a short transition, complete goblet squat 3 x 10 at 12 kg, light Romanian deadlift 2 x 10 with a load that permits a perfect hip hinge and neutral back, glute bridge 3 x 12, lat pulldown 3 x 10 at 40-50 kg, machine chest press 2 x 10 at a light controlled load, and Pallof press 3 x 10 per side. Stop any lift that causes back symptoms. Finish with at least 8 minutes of hip and hamstring mobility.

sessions.title: Conditional easy run/walk
sessions.description: Only if legs feel fresh and there is no unusual soreness or back discomfort: on a flat, forgiving route, warm up with 5 minutes of walking, then complete 5 rounds of 4 minutes very easy jogging and 1 minute walking. Keep HR below 145 bpm and the jog conversational. Cool down with 5 minutes of walking and perform gentle hip mobility. If recovery is incomplete, replace the jogging rounds with 25 minutes of easy walking rather than postponing the run to another day.

sessions.title: Back-safe full-body gym session
sessions.description: Warm up with 5 minutes of easy rowing below HR 125 and controlled hip-hinge practice. Complete goblet squat 3 x 10 at 12 kg, Romanian deadlift 3 x 8 with the same light load used Wednesday only if technique and back response were good, glute bridge 3 x 12, lat pulldown 3 x 10 at 40-50 kg, machine chest press 3 x 10 at a light load, Pallof press 3 x 10 per side, and front plank 3 x 20-30 seconds. Leave at least 3-4 repetitions in reserve and never lift through back pain. Finish with 10 minutes of hip-flexor, hamstring, and glute mobility.

sessions.title: Short steady outdoor ride
sessions.description: If conditions are dry, use the road or gravel bike with suitable tires and power meter for a relaxed outdoor ride. After 10-15 minutes easy, hold approximately 130-155 W on flatter sections, keeping HR below 145 bpm and avoiding hard climbing or sprinting. Do not chase power on steep or slippery sections. If outdoor conditions are unsuitable, ride indoors at 135-150 W with the same steady intent. Finish with 8-10 minutes of hip mobility.

sessions.title: Easy weekend hike
sessions.description: Choose a moderate route and keep the entire outing conversational, generally below HR 135-140 bpm. Shorten strides or walk steep pitches rather than surging, and keep any summit or food stops brief. This is endurance and movement practice, not a long mountain challenge; turn around early if legs, back, or energy deteriorate. Include a small planned snack if needed and finish with relaxed hip and hamstring mobility.

week.rationale: Monday is reserved for recovery before training resumes with two short steady rides, two back-safe gym sessions, one beginner rowing exposure, one conditional run/walk, and a controlled weekend hike. Total planned training is about seven hours, with no formal cycling intensity and no additional long mountain outing. Cycling remains steady below the estimated 220 W FTP, strength progresses only through technically repeatable loads, and running is replaced by walking if hiking soreness persists. Each session has a distinct role: aerobic consistency, strength and position resilience, movement variety, or weekend endurance. Daily hip and hamstring mobility and repeatable dinner and evening-snack routines support long-ride comfort and gradual fat loss without aggressive restriction.

today.title: Recovery and mobility
today.description: Take a full training rest day after the long-hike load. A relaxed 10-20-minute walk is fine if it reduces stiffness, but do not count it as training or add another workout. Complete 10 minutes of gentle hip-flexor, hamstring, glute, and thoracic mobility without forcing end ranges. Eat a normal protein-containing dinner and prepare a planned evening snack to avoid grazing.
today.rationale: Rest is the best choice today because the first training adaptation this week is recovery from the long hike, not additional calorie burning or aerobic volume. Keeping today genuinely easy protects the quality of Tuesday's steady ride and Wednesday's first rowing-and-strength combination while reducing the risk that residual soreness provokes back compensation.
today.optionalRationale: Not applicable because today is a planned recovery day rather than an optional workout.

tomorrow.description: Use the trainer in ERG mode if your legs are adequately recovered. Keep HR approximately 125-145 bpm and avoid surges; reduce power if HR drifts above this range. Finish with 8-10 minutes of hip-flexor and hamstring mobility. If hike soreness remains substantial, replace the ride with 25-30 minutes of very easy walking rather than forcing the power targets.
alternatives: If substantial hiking soreness remains, take 25-30 minutes of very easy walking and keep the ride out of the week rather than moving it to Wednesday.
If 140-150 W causes HR to rise above 145 bpm despite steady breathing, reduce the main-set power to 125-140 W.
tomorrow.rationale: This is the week's first controlled aerobic stimulus: long enough to restart consistent fat oxidation and cycling-specific aerobic work, but well below the estimated 220 W FTP so it does not compromise the two strength sessions. A smooth power and HR line also rebuilds the steady pacing needed for long randonneur rides.

Skipping it without replacing it because of soreness would leave the week with only one ride and remove an important low-fatigue aerobic stimulus; replacing it with walking when sore preserves recovery without pretending that a forced ride would be productive.

blocks.name: Rebuild and Fat-Loss Foundation
blocks.focus: Re-establish training consistency with mostly easy aerobic cycling, short run-walk work, hiking, and technique-first gym sessions. blocks.name: Pole-Vault Preparation
blocks.focus: Maintain aerobic fitness with easy cycling and winter activities while shifting part of the gym program toward posterior-chain strength, controlled sprinting, landing mechanics, and low-volume explosive work. blocks.name: Pole-Vault Taper and Championship
blocks.focus: Reduce overall training volume while retaining brief technical vault sessions and a small number of high-quality sprint exposures. Maintain easy aerobic activity, avoid fatigue, and use the final week primarily for recovery, mobility, and competition readiness.

blocks.name: Post-Competition Recovery and Aerobic Rebuild
blocks.focus: Recover from the championship and rebuild steady aerobic volume with indoor cycling, easy outdoor riding when conditions permit, walking or hiking, and light strength work. blocks.name: Winter Aerobic Base
blocks.focus: Develop the primary endurance base through steady indoor cycling, fatbike riding, cross-country skiing, snowshoeing, hiking, and controlled rowing. Keep most cycling at low-to-moderate intensity with power targets, maintain a beginner running progression, and use gym sessions for back resilience, mobility, and general strength.

blocks.name: Spring Build and 200 km Brevet
blocks.focus: Increase aerobic volume and introduce structured threshold and longer endurance work as outdoor road conditions improve. Build climbing-specific strength and pacing skills, progress running and rowing, and use the April 200 km brevet as a key fitness checkpoint with conservative pacing and adequate fueling.

blocks.name: Paris-Brest-Paris Specific Build
blocks.focus: Convert the base into race-specific fitness with long rides, repeated climbing efforts, endurance intervals, fuelling practice, and bike setup optimization. blocks.focus: Reduce volume by roughly 30-50% while retaining race rhythm through short, sharp efforts and brief high-intensity sessions. Prioritize sleep, nutrition, hydration, mobility, and mental preparation, with a final long ride that rehearses equipment, pacing, and fuelling without creating fatigue.

season.rationale: The athlete is returning after substantial detraining but retains a strong endurance history, including a successful 1130 km bikepacking race. The season therefore begins with a short, low-stress rebuild that establishes consistency, protects the back, and supports gradual fat loss without creating the overtraining pattern the athlete has previously experienced. The January pole-vault championship is treated as a distinct priority, with a brief strength-and-sprint preparation and taper, followed by recovery and a renewed aerobic base. The spring build progressively increases volume and introduces controlled intensity, culminating in the April 200 km brevet. The final eight-week block develops race-specific endurance and climbing power, followed by a three-week taper for Paris-Brest-Paris. All blocks are contiguous, with no unnecessary high-intensity volume before the athlete is physiologically and technically prepared for it.

block.rationale: The athlete is returning after substantial detraining and has shown that consistency, not intensity, is the main limitation. The block therefore keeps most aerobic work easy and controlled, progresses duration gradually, and uses strength work to improve posterior-chain resilience and hip mobility without provoking the athlete's back problems. The 1 November hike is retained as a controlled aerobic checkpoint, while the 2027 pole-vault world championship adds a need for short sprint exposures, plyometrics, technical vault work, and careful posterior-chain loading. These elements are introduced gradually and kept low-volume so they support the later preparation block without undermining aerobic rebuilding or recreating the athlete's previous pattern of early burnout. sessions.title: Recovery and hip mobility
sessions.description: No structured workout. Complete 20 minutes of gentle mobility only: seated hip-flexor and hamstring stretches, thoracic rotations, and easy walking. Keep the effort easy and stop if the back or hips become painful.

sessions.title: Easy indoor aerobic ride
sessions.description: Indoor bike with a 10-minute easy warm-up, then 30 minutes of steady riding at 120-140 W and HR 115-135 bpm, followed by a 5-10-minute cool-down. Keep cadence comfortable and avoid surges. If the legs feel heavy after Sunday's hike, reduce the main block to 20-25 minutes.

sessions.title: Short easy run-walk
sessions.description: Only if the legs feel fresh and there is no back or hip pain. Run 4 minutes at an easy conversational effort, then walk 1 minute, repeating for 20-25 minutes. Keep HR below 140 bpm and stop if the run-walk feels labored.

sessions.title: Technique-focused gym session
sessions.description: Spend 40-45 minutes on controlled strength work. Do 3 sets of 10 goblet squats at 12 kg if pain-free, 2 sets of 8 light Romanian deadlifts with a pain-free hip hinge, 3 sets of 12 glute bridges, 2 sets of 8-12 lat pulldowns, and 2 sets of 10 Pallof presses per side. Finish with 10-15 minutes of hip and thoracic mobility. Do not add deadlift load or extra squat sets if technique deteriorates.

sessions.title: Steady indoor aerobic ride
sessions.description: Indoor bike with a 10-minute warm-up, then 35-40 minutes at 130-150 W with HR 120-140 bpm, followed by a 5-10-minute cool-down. Aim for a smooth, flat effort rather than intervals. If HR rises more than about 10 bpm above target, reduce power immediately.

sessions.title: Rest, walking, and mobility
sessions.description: No structured workout. Take an easy 20-30 minute walk if comfortable and perform 15-20 minutes of gentle hip, hamstring, and thoracic mobility. Prioritize sleep, hydration, and normal meals without trying to compensate for the upcoming hike with extra training.

sessions.title: Controlled 5-hour hike
sessions.description: Complete the planned 5-hour hike at a steady, sustainable hiking pace. Keep HR mostly between 110 and 130 bpm, walk steep sections rather than running them, and limit summit stops to about 5 minutes. Carry sufficient water and food, and turn back or shorten the route if back, hip, or knee symptoms develop.

week.rationale: The 25 October mountain hike was substantially harder than the planned easy run-walk, so the first two days are deliberately light rather than adding intensity. The week retains the 1 November 5-hour hike as the main aerobic checkpoint, but keeps the surrounding cycling, running, and gym work easy and technically controlled. This protects the back and hips, supports fat-loss habits through regular movement, and avoids repeating the surge-recover pattern from the recent spinning classes. Short, low-volume vault preparation will be introduced gradually in the following weeks, with the main pole-vault emphasis beginning in the dedicated preparation block.

season.goal: Build toward Paris-Brest-Paris in August 2027, with a strong 200 km brevet in April 2027, improved general cycling fitness for longer road races, gradual fat loss from 24.5% to approximately 15% body fat, better hip mobility and back resilience, and foundational running, rowing, and strength training while preparing for the pole-vault world championship on 2027-01-07.

season.rationale: Because you historically sustain strict, disciplined training for a maximum of 3–4 months before burning out, the overarching strategy reserves high-discipline, structured cycling intervals and brevet-specific volume for the March–August 2027 window. However, with the newly added Pole Vault World Championship on January 7, 2027, the autumn and early winter are split into two focused phases: first, a 6-week anatomical adaptation, fat-loss habit, and running/rowing foundation block that safely prepares your lower back and hips for explosive loading; second, a 5-week vault-specific power, sprint conditioning, and technical taper block through early January. Once the vault championship concludes, January and February shift to low-stress Norwegian winter cross-training (cross-country skiing, snowshoeing, fatbiking, and indoor rowing) paired with heavy gym strength and steady caloric deficit to drive fat loss and aerobic base without mental fatigue. In March, as tarmac opens, we launch the disciplined 4-month cycling build: progressing FTP from ~220 W back toward 280+ W for the April 200 km brevet, expanding endurance through the May/June 300/400/600 km qualifiers and tour races, taking a brief mental and physical reset in July to prevent stagnation, and executing a final ultra-distance sharpening and taper for Paris-Brest-Paris in August.

sessions.description: Make-up session for last Sunday's missed run/walk—perform this as a run/walk ONLY if your legs and lower back feel completely fresh after Sunday's hike; if your quads or calves are still sore, convert this to a brisk 30-minute flat walk. sessions.title: Gym Strength Session 1: Goblet Squat Progression & RDL Intro
sessions.description: Warm-up: 8 minutes easy indoor rowing (keep HR strictly < 130 bpm, focusing on driving with the legs first and hinging at the hips with a flat back, 18–20 strokes/min). Main Strength Circuit (rest 90s between sets, stop any set immediately if lower-back form degrades): 1) Goblet Squat: 1 warm-up set of 10 reps at 4 kg, then 3 working sets of 10 reps at 12 kg (adding the 3rd set you skipped last week). 2) Dumbbell or Barbell Romanian Deadlift (RDL): 3x10 reps with very light load (e.g., 2x8–10 kg dumbbells or an empty 20 kg bar)—push hips straight back with a slight knee bend, keep spine neutral, and stop the descent mid-shin as soon as your hamstrings reach tension (never round your lower back to touch the floor). 3) Supine Glute Bridge: 3x12 reps with a 3-second isometric squeeze at the top (add a 10 kg plate on hips since bodyweight felt easy last week). 4) Lat Pulldown: 1x12 at 35 kg, then 3x10 at 50 kg. 5) Pallof Press: 3x10 reps per side with a 2-second hold at full extension. 6) Front Plank: 3x30 seconds with 45s rest (brace glutes and abs hard). Optional: 10–12 minutes of light technical pole vault drills (keep purely technical and playful, not fatiguing). Cool-down: Mandatory 10 minutes of hip flexor, hamstring, and adductor stretching (up from last week's 2.5 minutes).

sessions.title: Steady Zone 2 Indoor Cycling (140–150 W)
sessions.description: Use ERG mode on the indoor trainer to build on last weekend's ultra-steady rides. Warm-up: 10 minutes ramping smoothly from 100 W to 135 W. Main set: 40 minutes locked at 140–150 W (roughly 64–68% of your estimated 220 W FTP) with cadence at 85–95 rpm. Cool-down: 10 minutes easy spinning at 100–115 W. Target HR is 120–138 bpm (strict ceiling of 142 bpm). The goal is a completely flat power and heart rate trace with zero surges, training fat oxidation and aerobic efficiency without adding recovery debt ahead of the weekend.

sessions.title: Gym Strength Session 2: Hinge Technique, Anti-Extension Core & Mobility
sessions.description: Keep leg loads controlled today so you have 48 hours to recover before Sunday's 5-hour hike. Warm-up: 8 minutes easy indoor rowing (< 130 bpm, smooth leg-hip-arm sequence). Main Strength Circuit: 1) Romanian Deadlift (RDL): 3x10 reps at the same light, strict weight used Wednesday—focus 100% on feeling the stretch in the hamstrings while keeping the lower back locked flat. 2) Goblet Squat: 2x10 reps at 12 kg (capped at 2 sets today to save quads for Sunday). 3) Seated Cable Row (neutral grip): 3x12 reps at 40–45 kg, pausing 1s at the chest with shoulder blades retracted. 4) Single-Leg Glute Bridge (or elevated 2-leg bridge): 3x8 reps per side to build pelvic stability for cycling and vault takeoffs. 5) Dead Bug (core anti-extension for back protection and pole vault plant): 3x8 slow, controlled reps per side, pressing your lower back firmly into the mat throughout. 6) Bird-Dog: 3x8 reps per side with a 3-second hold. Cool-down: 12 minutes of dedicated lower-body mobility (90/90 hip switches, couch stretch, and doorway hamstring stretch).

sessions.title: Pre-Hike Rest & Mobility Day
sessions.description: Complete rest day—do not add an unplanned indoor ride like last Saturday, as tomorrow's 5-hour mountain hike is the cornerstone endurance session of this week. Spend 15 minutes doing gentle hip and thoracic spine mobility, prepare your hiking gear, hydration, and pocket nutrition for tomorrow, and stick to a normal, balanced dinner without overeating.

sessions.title: Long Endurance Mountain Hike (5 Hours)
sessions.description: Planned 5-hour mountain hike to build deep aerobic durability and fat oxidation. Pacing & HR discipline: Unlike last Sunday's Selbu hike where climbs pushed your HR into the 150s–160s, shorten your stride and slow your cadence on steep pitches to keep your heart rate strictly between 110 and 135 bpm (absolute ceiling 140 bpm). Stop discipline: Keep summit or view breaks under 5–10 minutes so your body stays warm and in continuous aerobic rhythm. Fueling for fat loss: Eat a solid breakfast before departing, carry water/electrolytes and ~25–30 g of slow carbohydrates per hour (e.g., a small sandwich, banana, or oat bar) during the hike so you do not return home with an extreme caloric deficit that triggers a Sunday night kitchen binge.

week.rationale: Because you replaced last Sunday's planned 30-minute run/walk with a demanding 2h45 mountain hike (608 m climbing, HR into the 160s) on top of back-to-back indoor rides on Friday and Saturday, your legs carry much more muscular fatigue into this week than originally planned. To protect your lower back and ensure you are fresh for Sunday's 5-hour hike on November 1, Monday is set as a complete rest day (with daily hip mobility) and the delayed 30-minute run/walk is placed on Tuesday as an optional/convertible session depending on leg freshness. In the gym on Wednesday and Friday, we build directly on last Thursday's feedback: adding the third set of 12 kg goblet squats, introducing very light Romanian deadlifts (RDLs) with a strict hip hinge to safely prepare your posterior chain for both cycling posture and your newly announced January 7 Pole Vault World Championship, and extending post-workout stretching from 2.5 minutes to a dedicated 10–12 minutes. Thursday's indoor ride nudges your steady target up slightly to 140–150 W while keeping the same flat, surge-free heart rate line (120–138 bpm) you executed so well on October 23 and 24. Saturday is a full rest day so you can execute Sunday's 5-hour hike with disciplined pacing and stop control. For your fat-loss goal this week, combat the post-work hunger trap by drinking a large glass of water and eating a high-protein, high-fiber snack 30 minutes before leaving work, and brush your teeth immediately after dinner to create a clear mental barrier against late-evening kitchen snacking.

season.goal: Achieve sustainable fat loss from 24.5% toward 15% body fat, resolve hip mobility and lower-back durability limitations through progressive gym strength training, prepare safely for the January 7 Pole Vault World Championship, and build cycling fitness to complete the 2027 spring/summer brevet qualifiers (starting with a 200 km in April), competitive tour races, and Paris-Brest-Paris (1200 km) in August 2027.

blocks.name: Rebuild, Hip Mobility & Vault Conditioning Base
blocks.focus: Establish sustainable fat-loss nutrition habits, progressive lower-back and hip-hinge strength in the gym, daily hip flexibility work, steady Zone 2 aerobic base (indoor cycling, hiking, beginner rowing), and a gradual return-to-running progression to prepare tendons and musculature for sprint and pole vault loading.

blocks.name: Pole Vault Championship Specificity & Taper
blocks.focus: Transition gym work to explosive posterior-chain power, core anti-extension strength, short sprint mechanics, and technical pole vault sessions while tapering volume into the January 7 World Championship. Maintain easy indoor cycling and winter outdoor movement as low-stress supporting volume for ongoing weight management.

blocks.name: Norwegian Winter Multi-Sport Base & Fat Loss
blocks.focus: Low-mental-strain winter aerobic volume utilizing cross-country skiing, snowshoeing, studded-tire fatbiking, indoor rowing, and 5K running progression. Prioritize consistent gym strength and core durability alongside steady fat loss while saving strict cycling discipline for the spring.

blocks.name: Spring Cycling Build & 200km Brevet Prep
blocks.focus: Initiate the disciplined cycling phase as roads clear in March. Introduce structured ERG-mode sweet-spot and threshold intervals to raise FTP toward 280 W, transition gym work to strength maintenance, and build outdoor tarmac endurance to comfortably complete the April 200 km brevet.

blocks.name: Brevet Series Progression & Tour Race Fitness
blocks.focus: Extend long-ride durability, bike posture comfort, and metabolic efficiency for the 300 km, 400 km, and 600 km qualifying brevets, interspersed with targeted VO2max and threshold sharpening to ride competitively in longer amateur tour races.

blocks.name: Mid-Summer Recovery & Mental Reset
blocks.focus: Deliberate reduction in structured training density after the 600 km qualifier to shed cumulative physical fatigue, prevent the 4-month burnout ceiling, and refresh motivation via unstructured scenic rides, hiking, and mobility before the final PBP push.

blocks.name: Paris-Brest-Paris Specificity & Taper
blocks.focus: Final ultra-endurance volume simulation, night-riding and fueling rehearsals, and lower-back/contact-point preservation, followed by a structured 2-week taper to arrive at the August Paris-Brest-Paris start line completely fresh, lean, and resilient.

season.rationale: Because you historically sustain strict, disciplined training for a maximum of 3–4 months before burning out, the overarching strategy reserves high-discipline, structured cycling intervals and brevet-specific volume for the March–August 2027 window. However, with the newly added Pole Vault World Championship on January 7, 2027, the autumn and early winter are split into two focused phases: first, a 6-week anatomical adaptation, fat-loss habit, and running/rowing foundation block that safely prepares your lower back and hips for explosive loading; second, a 5-week vault-specific power, sprint conditioning, and technical taper block through early January. Once the vault championship concludes, January and February shift to low-stress Norwegian winter cross-training (cross-country skiing, snowshoeing, fatbiking, and indoor rowing) paired with heavy gym strength and steady caloric deficit to drive fat loss and aerobic base without mental fatigue. In March, as tarmac opens, we launch the disciplined 4-month cycling build: progressing FTP from ~220 W back toward 280+ W for the April 200 km brevet, expanding endurance through the May/June 300/400/600 km qualifiers and tour races, taking a brief mental and physical reset in July to prevent stagnation, and executing a final ultra-distance sharpening and taper for Paris-Brest-Paris in August.

sessions.title: Gym Strength A: Hinge Introduction, Squat Progression & Hip Mobility

sessions.description: Steady aerobic ride on the indoor trainer using ERG mode or flat virtual terrain. Warm-up: 10 minutes building gradually from 100 W to 135 W. Cool-down: 5 minutes easy spinning at 100–110 W.

sessions.title: Beginner Run/Walk Progression & Tendon Prep
sessions.description: Headlamp run on a flat, predictable surface (gravel path or tarmac) to build lower-leg and Achilles resilience ahead of pole vault runway work. Warm-up: 5 minutes brisk walking + gentle ankle circles and leg swings. Main set: 6 rounds of (3 minutes easy jogging / 1 minute brisk walk) = 24 minutes. Keep running cadence light and quick with short strides; cap HR strictly below 142 bpm (if HR climbs higher, slow the jog pace). Cool-down: 6 minutes easy walk, followed by 5 minutes of calf and hip-flexor stretching indoors.

sessions.title: Beginner Indoor Rowing Session 1 & Hip Mobility
sessions.description: Introduction to structured indoor rowing on the ergometer. Set damper to 3–4 (drag factor ~110–120) to protect your lower back. Focus on sequence: Legs -> Hips -> Arms on the drive (1 count), and Arms -> Hips -> Legs on the recovery (2 counts)—never round the lower back at the catch. Warm-up: 5 minutes easy rowing at 18–20 strokes per minute (spm), HR < 125 bpm. Main set: 4 x 5 minutes at 20–22 spm with 90 seconds easy rest/paddle between intervals; keep HR in the steady Zone 2 range (125–140 bpm). Finish with 10 minutes of floor hip mobility and thoracic spine rotations.

sessions.title: Gym Strength B & Technical Pole Vault Play
sessions.description: Warm-up: 8 minutes on the indoor staircase machine or rower (HR < 130 bpm) + dynamic hip openers. Strength Block: 1) Goblet Squat: 3x10 at 12–14 kg (only move to 14 kg if Tuesday's 3x10 at 12 kg caused minimal soreness). 2) Glute Bridge: 3x12 with a 10–15 kg weight plate or dumbbell across hips, holding 2 seconds at the top. 3) Seated Cable Row or Dumbbell Row: 3x10–12 (40–45 kg). 4) Deadbug (core anti-extension for vaulting & back safety): 3x8 slow reps per side, pressing lower back firmly into the mat. Technical Vault & Mobility: 10–15 minutes of light, playful pole vault drills/plant mechanics (keep intensity playful and submaximal) + 10 minutes of hip flexor and hamstring stretching.

sessions.title: Weekend Aerobic Endurance: Mountain Hike or Fatbike Ride
sessions.description: Low-stress weekend Zone 2 endurance session—choose either a scenic mountain/forest hike or an outdoor ride on your fatbike or gravel bike depending on trail conditions. Maintain a steady aerobic effort with average HR between 115 and 135 bpm, and cap steep uphill efforts at 142 bpm by shortening your stride (hiking) or shifting to your easiest gears (cycling). Practice stop discipline: keep any summit or turnaround pauses under 5 minutes so your core body temperature and aerobic stimulus stay steady.

week.rationale: Because no workouts were logged during Week 1 (2026-10-26 to 2026-11-01), you are entering Week 2 completely rested following the October 25 mountain hike, rather than carrying fatigue from a 5-hour November 1 hike. This week picks up the exact anatomical progressions planned for your next gym step: adding the third goblet squat set at 12 kg, introducing light Romanian deadlifts (RDLs) with a strict hip hinge, and dedicating a full 10–12 minutes to hip mobility at the end of sessions (up from 2.5 minutes). We also introduce your requested beginner indoor rowing program and beginner run/walk intervals to safely condition your Achilles and hamstrings for upcoming sprint/vault work, alongside a steady 140–150 W indoor ride and a 2-hour weekend hike or fatbike outing.

season.goal: Achieve gradual fat loss, improve back-tolerant strength and hip mobility, prepare safely for the reported 7 January pole-vault championship, complete the 2027 brevet qualification series comfortably, and finish Paris-Brest-Paris strongly while maintaining fitness for longer cycling races.

blocks.name: Recovery and sustainable re-entry
blocks.focus: Begin with several easy days after the 25 October hike. Initially target approximately 4–6 total hours weekly, including hiking and strength rather than adding them on top. Shorten or skip the planned 1 November hike if recovery is incomplete. Ride easily around 110–145 W using provisional FTP 220 W, reducing power when needed to remain conversational. For other activities, use conversational effort and provisionally 115–135 bpm, recognizing that sport-specific HR zones are untested. Start two short gym sessions with 1–2 sets of 8–12 comfortable repetitions of supported squat or leg press, glute bridge, supported row, pulldown and chest press, plus Pallof press and short side planks. Leave several repetitions in reserve. Seek assessment for recurrent back pain and clarify January competition details.

blocks.name: Flexible winter foundation
blocks.focus: Build toward approximately 5–7 hours weekly only with good recovery. Combine two easy cycling exposures, two back-tolerant gym sessions and an enjoyable hike, ski, snowshoe or fatbike outing, substituting rather than accumulating activities. Introduce one short run/walk session weekly, progressing toward two only when comfortable. Start rowing with 10–15-minute technique-led bouts; avoid rapidly increasing both new sports together. Add 5–10 minutes of comfortable hip mobility most days without forcing lumbar flexion. If January participation is confirmed, supervised vault practice replaces other work, with approach and landing competence established before explosive progression. Introduce at most one brief controlled cycling intensity session weekly when recovered.

blocks.name: January event preparation
blocks.focus: If participation is confirmed and preparation judged safe, prioritize supervised vault technique and low-volume event-specific efforts with full recovery. Avoid unsupervised maximal sprinting, depth jumps and heavy good mornings. Maintain endurance through two mostly easy cycling sessions, keeping total training near a sustainable 5–7 hours instead of adding vault work on top. Progress strength only with sound technique and no worsening back symptoms. Otherwise continue the flexible winter foundation. Reduce loading in the final week and avoid aggressive fat loss.

blocks.name: January competition and recovery
blocks.focus: For the reported 7 January championship, substantially reduce volume and retain only brief familiar technical work under the vault coach. Avoid new exercises and soreness-producing lifting. Prioritize sleep, carbohydrate availability and adequate energy intake. Follow competition with several easy days and assess back, tendon and general fatigue before resuming training. If the event is not confirmed, use this as a low-load winter recovery week.

blocks.name: Winter aerobic development and strength
blocks.focus: Progress toward 6–8 hours weekly through easy cycling, skiing, snowshoeing and hiking, with two gym sessions and at least one low-load day. Preserve regular cycling specificity, including an indoor session. Once recovered, reassess cycling threshold using a familiar controlled test and update power zones rather than relying on historical FTP. Introduce one weekly controlled tempo or threshold session. Progress run/walk toward 30 minutes of comfortable continuous running and rowing toward 20–30 easy minutes without compromising recovery. Keep outdoor sessions within two hours below -15 C. Include easier weeks approximately every third or fourth week.

blocks.name: Road transition and 200 km readiness
blocks.focus: Shift toward three cycling sessions weekly as roads permit, with approximately 7–10 total hours when sustainable. Gradually extend the long ride toward 4–6 hours, interspersing easier weekends. Retain one controlled quality session and one or two reduced-volume gym sessions. Most endurance riding stays around 60–70% of reassessed FTP, moderated by effort on climbs. Practice 40–60 g carbohydrate/hour, progressing toward 60–90 g/hour as tolerated for longer rides. Arrange bike-fit and saddle assessments; flexibility alone will not resolve skin injury or back pain. Prepare for the April 200 km brevet as a comfortable completion goal, adjusting the final days around its confirmed date.

blocks.name: Brevet qualification and cycling performance
blocks.focus: Complete the 200/300/400/600 km series according to organizer dates and qualification deadlines. Use the brevets as the principal ultra-distance progression rather than adding frequent very long training rides. Ordinary weeks may reach 8–12 hours if recovery permits; event weeks require reduced training beforehand and several recovery days afterward. Maintain one threshold or aerobic-power session only in well-recovered weeks and one weekly strength-maintenance session. A longer tour race replaces a hard session or long ride rather than supplementing a brevet week. Refine pacing, fueling, navigation, lights, clothing, stops and sleep strategy. Reduce or suspend the calorie deficit as demands increase.

blocks.name: Midseason recovery and motivational reset
blocks.focus: Reduce training for approximately two weeks after qualification, adjusting recovery timing if the final brevet occurs later. Choose enjoyable easy cycling, walking, light rowing, gentle mobility and light strength. Avoid chasing missed workouts or fitness tests. Review saddle skin health, back tolerance, appetite, sleep and motivation, and finalize August equipment and logistics.

blocks.name: Paris-Brest-Paris specificity
blocks.focus: Use a focused four-week block, generally around 9–13 hours in ordinary weeks only if supported by spring training. Emphasize comfortable riding position, economical rolling-terrain pacing, night-equipment checks and efficient stops. Include one carefully placed back-to-back endurance weekend or longer rehearsal, not a full event-distance simulation, completing the largest load at least three weeks before the event.
