sessions.title: Recover from Sunday's mountain hike
sessions.description: No structured training. Sunday's 165-minute hike with 608 m climbing followed Saturday's approximately 60-minute easy ride. Do not make up the run/walk or add lifting. Prioritize sleep, regular meals and hydration; assess leg soreness, stair descent and back comfort.

sessions.title: Gentle recovery walk and hip mobility
sessions.description: If soreness is improving and walking is normal, walk 15 minutes on flat ground at RPE 1–2/10, generally below 125 bpm without chasing a heart-rate target. Follow with 5 minutes of comfortable hip rotations and gentle hip-flexor stretches. Avoid forced hamstring stretching or rounding the lower back. Replace with rest if fatigue remains pronounced or walking alters your gait.

sessions.title: Easy cycling re-entry
sessions.description: Ride 40 minutes: 8 minutes at 90–110 W, 27 minutes at 110–135 W and 5 minutes below 110 W. Finish with 5 minutes of gentle hip mobility. Using provisional FTP 220 W, keep RPE 2–3/10 and full-sentence conversation. Reduce power if HR stays above approximately 135–140 bpm or legs feel heavy; do not increase power to reach an HR target. Choose a flat outdoor route, using lights as needed given your comfort riding in darkness; substitute the trainer if conditions are unsafe. This restores cycling-specific aerobic consistency without interval fatigue.

sessions.title: Back-tolerant introductory gym strength
sessions.description: Warm up with 5 minutes of cycling below 110 W. Perform one set each: squat to bench, bodyweight or 4 kg, 8–10 reps; glute bridge 10–12; chest-supported row 10–12; lat pulldown 10–12, starting around 30 kg if comfortable; machine chest press 8–12; Pallof press 8–10/side. Add knee-supported side plank 2 x 10–15 seconds/side. Rest 60–90 seconds and leave 4–5 repetitions in reserve, selecting light loads accordingly. Finish with 5 minutes of comfortable hip mobility. No loaded hinges, heavy squats or vaulting. This establishes whole-body and trunk load tolerance for prolonged cycling posture. Stop painful exercises; seek physiotherapy assessment for recurrent back pain.

sessions.title: Steady easy cycling
sessions.description: Ride 45 minutes on a familiar flat or gently rolling route: 8 minutes at 90–110 W, 32 minutes mainly at 110–140 W and 5 minutes easy. Finish with 5 minutes of hip mobility. Keep RPE 2–3/10, shift early and avoid surges; reduce power if HR stays above approximately 135–140 bpm or fatigue persists. Use effective lights and appropriate tires. Substitute the same ride on the trainer if conditions are unsafe. This second cycling exposure reinforces aerobic efficiency and steady brevet pacing without extending the recovery week's load.

sessions.title: Conditional light gym rehearsal
sessions.description: Proceed only if Thursday caused no meaningful soreness, back symptoms are unchanged and normal walking is comfortable; otherwise rest. Warm up 5 minutes on the bike below 110 W. Perform one set each at Thursday's loads or lighter: squat to bench 8 reps, glute bridge 10, chest-supported row 10, lat pulldown 10, machine chest press 8–10 and Pallof press 8/side. Add knee-supported side plank 2 x 10 seconds/side. Rest 60–90 seconds and leave 4–5 reps in reserve. Finish with gentle mobility within 30 minutes. This reinforces movement skills and assesses strength tolerance without progressing load. Skipping costs only a small technique exposure and is preferable to compromising recovery or Sunday's hike.

sessions.title: Short, easy endurance hike
sessions.description: Only if fatigue has resolved and descending stairs is comfortable, hike 80 minutes on an easy route with modest climbing and an early turnaround, then spend 5 minutes on gentle mobility. Keep RPE 2–3/10 and full-sentence conversation; provisional HR guidance is 115–135 bpm, not a target to chase. Slow on climbs and take safety or comfort breaks as needed. This supplies low-intensity endurance time supporting the cycling foundation without repeating last Sunday's stress. Do not extend to five hours. If tired, substitute a 20–30-minute flat walk or rest. Bring a snack, fluids and suitable layers; below -15 °C keep total outdoor exposure under two hours.

week.rationale: The latest activity record supersedes the earlier review: Sunday included a substantial hike, and Saturday added approximately 60 minutes of cycling. season.goal: Achieve gradual fat loss, improve back-tolerant strength and hip mobility, prepare safely for the reported 7 January pole-vault championship, complete the 2027 brevet qualification series comfortably, and finish Paris-Brest-Paris strongly while maintaining fitness for longer cycling races.

blocks.name: Flexible winter foundation

Arrange bike-fit and saddle assessments; flexibility alone will not resolve skin injury or back pain. Prepare for the April 200 km brevet as a comfortable completion goal, adjusting the final days around its confirmed date.

blocks.name: Brevet qualification and cycling performance

No loaded hinges or painful movements. This establishes strength and trunk-control tolerance for sustained cycling posture; skipping it removes one of two weekly practice exposures.

sessions.description: Ride outdoors for 45 minutes: 10 minutes at 90–115 W, 30 minutes at 110–145 W and 5 minutes very easy. Finish with 5 minutes of gentle hip mobility. This second cycling exposure maintains aerobic fitness and steady pacing for long brevets; skipping it leaves only one cycling stimulus this week.

sessions.description: Allow at least 48 hours after Wednesday's gym session. Warm up with 5 minutes of easy stationary cycling. Retain comfortable Wednesday loads, leave at least 4 repetitions in reserve and rest 60–90 seconds. Repeat a second set only where already tolerated without meaningful soreness. Finish with 6 minutes of gentle hip mobility within 40 minutes. Omit lower-body lifting if soreness alters movement; stop painful exercises. Seek clinical assessment for recurrent or worsening back pain. This repeat exposure reinforces movement skill and trunk endurance; skipping it reduces strength-practice frequency.

Stay outdoors less than two hours below -15 C. This is the week's longer continuous aerobic stimulus for eventual brevet durability and sustainable activity supporting fat loss; skipping it removes that duration exposure, but recovery takes priority.

season.goal: Prioritize gradual fat loss and back-resilient strength while preparing safely for the reported pole vault competition on 2027-01-07, comfortably completing the 2027 randonneur qualifying series beginning with a 200 km brevet in April, and finishing Paris-Brest-Paris strongly in August 2027. blocks.name: Recovery and sustainable re-entry
blocks.focus: Start with several genuinely easy days after the October 25 hike. Shorten or skip the planned November 1 five-hour hike if fatigue, soreness or back discomfort persists. Begin two conservative gym sessions using supported lower-body work, glute bridges, pulldowns, presses and Pallof presses, initially 1–2 sets of 8–12 controlled repetitions with several repetitions in reserve. Do not automatically add squat sets or Romanian deadlifts before technique and symptoms support progression. Add comfortable hip mobility and trunk endurance; seek physiotherapy assessment for recurrent back symptoms. Confirm January competition details and vault coaching.

blocks.name: Winter foundation and supervised vault preparation
blocks.focus: Build mostly easy aerobic consistency using trainer rides, skiing, snowshoeing, fatbike outings, hiking or staircase work; substitute activities rather than scheduling every sport each week. Maintain two gym sessions with gradual, symptom-free loading. If appropriately supervised, introduce vault technique and low-volume approach drills, with impact progression determined by competence and recovery. Begin one or two short run/walk exposures weekly, progressing duration before speed, and optional 10–20-minute rowing technique sessions. Separate demanding lower-body sessions by at least 48 hours. Below -15 C, keep outdoor sessions within two hours.

blocks.name: Vault-specific preparation with aerobic maintenance
blocks.focus: If the January event is confirmed and safe preparation is established, prioritize coached vault technique and modest approach-speed practice with full recovery. Plyometrics and heavier lifting depend on demonstrated tolerance and are not mandatory. Keep cycling and winter endurance predominantly easy and reduce competing lower-body fatigue. Avoid aggressive weight loss. If the vault event is not pursued, continue enjoyable winter foundation training instead of introducing unnecessary explosive work.

blocks.name: January competition taper and recovery
blocks.focus: Reduce training volume substantially while retaining brief, familiar technical work before the reported January 7 pole vault competition. Avoid new exercises, heavy leg loading and fatiguing endurance sessions. Compete only with appropriate technical readiness and symptom control, then take several easy recovery days. If the event is not confirmed, use this as a winter recovery week.

blocks.name: Flexible winter aerobic foundation
blocks.focus: Return to enjoyable multisport training with two cycling exposures most weeks, two back-tolerant gym sessions and easy skiing, snowshoeing or hiking. Progress run/walk toward a comfortable continuous 30-minute run only if impact is well tolerated. Continue beginner rowing with technique before resistance or duration. Introduce one controlled cycling tempo session weekly when recovered while keeping most endurance time easy. Continue gradual fat loss, monitoring weight trends, appetite and recovery without forcing progress.

blocks.name: Cycling build I: aerobic capacity and durability
blocks.focus: Begin focused cycling training with approximately three rides weekly: one controlled quality session, one easy ride and one progressively longer endurance ride. Start with tempo or short threshold intervals, then selectively introduce aerobic-power work rather than immediately adding a second hard day. Reassess FTP after consistent training. Maintain strength twice weekly if recovery allows; keep running and rowing optional and easy. Include a lighter final week and practice carbohydrate intake on rides exceeding two hours.

blocks.name: Road transition and 200 km preparation
blocks.focus: Move onto road and gravel as conditions permit. Progress the long ride toward approximately 4–6 hours only from demonstrated tolerance, combining steady endurance with occasional controlled climbing. Keep one purposeful midweek cycling intensity session and one or two strength sessions with reduced lower-body volume. Test saddle contact, clothing, hand positions, lighting and nutrition. Arrange a professional bike-fit review rather than assuming flexibility alone will resolve blisters or back pain. Practice 60–90 g carbohydrate per hour as tolerated and individualized hydration. Reduce training before the actual April 200 km brevet.

blocks.name: First brevet and sustainable qualifying progression
blocks.focus: Complete the April 200 km brevet at a controlled effort and assess pacing, contact-point comfort, fueling and recovery. Schedule several easy days afterward before resuming demanding training. Place a 300 km qualifier here only if its confirmed date and recovery permit; otherwise adjust subsequent blocks. Brevets replace the week's long training ride and usually its demanding interval session. Maintain one gym session and small doses of cycling intensity between events without chasing fatigue.

blocks.name: Long-brevet specificity and qualification
blocks.focus: Progress through confirmed 300 km and 400 km qualifiers with event-specific pacing, night-riding practice, reliable equipment and efficient stops. Introduce back-to-back endurance rides only when useful and recoverable. Retain one short threshold or aerobic-power session in non-event weeks for general cycling fitness. A longer tour race may replace that week's hard endurance session when well separated from a brevet. Maintain strength with low volume and avoid running progression during high cycling loads.

blocks.name: Final qualification and ultra-distance rehearsal
blocks.focus: Place the 600 km qualifier and any remaining qualifying event according to official deadlines and local dates. Validate realistic pacing, feeding, saddle management, luggage, visibility and sleep logistics without deliberately practicing unsafe sleep deprivation. Allow substantial recovery afterward, commonly a week or longer before demanding training depending on symptoms. Maintain fitness between events with easy rides and brief quality work rather than additional very long rides. Shift nutrition toward full training support rather than pursuing a weight deadline.

blocks.name: Midseason physical and motivational reset
blocks.focus: Take a deliberately low-load week after the qualifying series, extending recovery if needed. Use short easy rides, comfortable mobility and enjoyable non-cycling activities. Review qualification status, back and saddle symptoms, fueling success and motivation. Avoid fitness tests, compensatory training and mandatory long rides.

blocks.name: Cycling build II: Paris-Brest-Paris specificity
blocks.focus: Use a short final build emphasizing repeatable endurance, economical pacing and comfort over consecutive days. Include one cycling quality session most weeks, one long ride or carefully selected back-to-back weekend, and easy supporting rides. Include a lighter week. Rehearse the complete event setup and feeding plan without repeating a 600 km effort merely for reassurance. Finish the last demanding endurance weekend approximately three weeks before the event. Maintain strength once weekly without soreness and minimize competing running or hiking loads.

blocks.name: Taper and Paris-Brest-Paris
blocks.focus: Progressively reduce pre-event training volume by approximately 40–60% relative to the final build while retaining familiar ride frequency and brief, non-exhaustive intensity. Avoid heavy strength work, long hikes, running progression and last-minute equipment changes. Prioritize sleep, carbohydrate availability, travel logistics and saddle-skin health. Ride the provisionally scheduled August 22–26 Paris-Brest-Paris with conservative early pacing, practiced fueling and planned sleep. Adjust dates once the official schedule and athlete's start time are confirmed.

weeks.focus: Establish repeatable easy training and introduce brief rowing or run/walk only when recovered.

weeks.focus: Consolidate easy aerobic frequency and back-tolerant strength with a small, conditional duration increase.
weeks.targetLoad: Approximately 5–5.5 hours only if week 2 is well tolerated; otherwise repeat or reduce it. block.rationale: Keep the existing block dates and recovery-first purpose. week.focus: Recover from the weekend load, restore back-tolerant strength practice, and maintain easy endurance without accumulating fatigue.

sessions.title: Recover from Sunday's mountain hike
sessions.description: No structured training after Sunday's 165-minute hike with 608 m of climbing. Prioritize sleep, normal meals and hydration. Gentle, comfortable hip movements are fine; avoid forceful stretching. Assess walking, stairs and back comfort before resuming exercise.

sessions.title: Gentle recovery walk and hip mobility
sessions.description: Walk on flat ground for 15 minutes at RPE 1–2/10, with provisional HR below 120 bpm and no minimum target. Finish with 5 minutes of gentle supported hip rotations, hip-flexor stretching and comfortable hamstring mobility. Use lights and reflective clothing after dark. Rest instead if walking alters your gait or increases soreness or back discomfort. Skipping this small movement exposure is acceptable if recovery remains incomplete.

sessions.title: Gym A: conservative full-body re-entry
sessions.description: Proceed only if walking and stairs feel normal. Warm up 5 minutes on a gym bike at 70–100 W. Perform supported sit-to-stand or shallow leg press 1 x 8–10, glute bridge 1 x 10–12, lat pulldown 1 x 10 at approximately 30 kg or lighter, and machine chest press 1 x 8–12. Choose loads leaving 4–5 repetitions in reserve; rest 60–90 seconds. Add Pallof press 1 x 8/side and bird dog 1 x 5/side with 5-second holds. Finish with 5 minutes of comfortable hip mobility. This rebuilds strength tolerance and trunk control for cycling without chasing soreness. No loaded hinges, extra squat sets, jumping or vaulting. Omit painful movements; rest if symptoms persist.

sessions.title: Easy steady cycling and mobility
sessions.description: Ride outdoors on a flat route for 35 minutes: 8 minutes at 90–115 W, 22 minutes at 115–140 W, and 5 minutes very easy. Keep conversational RPE 2–3/10 and HR generally below approximately 135 bpm, without a minimum target. Avoid climbing surges. Finish with 5 minutes of comfortable hip mobility. This retains cycling-specific aerobic conditioning while limiting recovery cost. Use lights after work; use the same prescription on the trainer if conditions are unsafe.

sessions.title: Gym B: consolidate technique without progression
sessions.description: Start at least 48 hours after Wednesday's gym session. Warm up 5 minutes on a gym bike at 70–100 W. Repeat supported sit-to-stand or shallow leg press 1 x 8–10, glute bridge 1 x 10–12, lat pulldown 1 x 10 at Wednesday's comfortable load, and machine chest press 1 x 8–12. Retain 4–5 repetitions in reserve and rest 60–90 seconds. Add Pallof press 1 x 8/side and bird dog 1 x 5/side with 5-second holds, then 5 minutes of gentle mobility. This second exposure reinforces technique and back-tolerant strength rather than increasing load. If Wednesday caused lingering leg soreness, omit lower-body exercises; rest if recovery is generally incomplete.

sessions.title: Rest and assess readiness for hiking
sessions.description: No structured training or compensatory ride. Rest allows recovery from Friday's strength practice before Sunday's endurance exposure. Check footwear, layers, food and route exit options. Shorten or cancel Sunday's hike if fatigue, soreness or back discomfort persists.

sessions.title: Shortened conversational hike
sessions.description: Plan 80 minutes of easy hiking plus 5 minutes of comfortable mobility afterward, replacing the earlier five-hour proposal. Choose gentle terrain with little steep descending and an easy early exit. Start in daylight. Hold RPE 2–3/10 and provisional HR mostly 110–135 bpm; slow on climbs and take breaks as needed. This provides recoverable aerobic time on feet toward long-event durability. Reduce to 30–60 minutes on flat terrain or cancel if fatigue, altered gait or back pain remains. Carry a snack and fluids; avoid deliberate underfueling. Do not extend into a long social hike without reassessing recovery.

week.rationale: The October 24 ride and October 25 hike supersede the earlier review's incomplete account. Sunday's hike contributed approximately 165 moving minutes; elapsed time and activity comments are not additional training. Schedule a reduced 215-minute week including mobility, with two initial low-load days, two conservative gym exposures at least 48 hours apart, one steady ride and one shortened hike. Strength supports lean-mass retention during gradual fat loss and trunk endurance for long rides; cycling preserves sport-specific aerobic conditioning; hiking supplies recoverable aerobic time on feet. No running, loaded hinges, intervals or explosive work this week. Cancel rather than make up sessions if recovery lags. Confirm the January 7 vault event, experience and qualified supervision before adding vault preparation. Use regular protein-rich meals and a planned afternoon snack rather than underfueling exercise. Seek physiotherapy assessment for recurrent back symptoms; stop and seek assessment for sharp, radiating or worsening pain.

today.title: Recover from Sunday's mountain hike

today.rationale: Rest is the best choice after the substantial weekend load, allowing leg and back recovery before rebuilding strength and aerobic consistency. Adding training today would risk carrying fatigue into the rest of this recovery-first week. Do not make up the missed run/walk.

season.goal: Prioritize gradual fat loss and back-resilient strength while preparing safely for the reported pole vault competition on 2027-01-07, comfortably completing the 2027 randonneur qualifying series beginning with a 200 km brevet in April, and finishing Paris-Brest-Paris strongly in August 2027. Develop cycling fitness for occasional longer road races.

Begin two conservative gym sessions using supported lower-body work, glute bridges, pulldowns, presses and Pallof presses, initially 1–2 sets of 8–12 controlled repetitions with several repetitions in reserve. Do not automatically add squat sets or Romanian deadlifts before technique and symptoms support progression. Add comfortable hip mobility and trunk endurance; seek physiotherapy assessment for recurrent back symptoms. Confirm January competition details and vault coaching.

blocks.name: Winter foundation and supervised vault preparation
blocks.focus: Build mostly easy aerobic consistency using trainer rides, skiing, snowshoeing, fatbike outings, hiking or staircase work; substitute activities rather than scheduling every sport each week. Maintain two gym sessions with gradual, symptom-free loading. If appropriately supervised, introduce vault technique and low-volume approach drills, with impact progression determined by competence and recovery. Begin one or two short run/walk exposures weekly, progressing duration before speed, and optional 10–20-minute rowing technique sessions. Separate demanding lower-body sessions by at least 48 hours. Below -15 C, keep outdoor sessions within two hours.

blocks.name: Vault-specific preparation with aerobic maintenance
blocks.focus: If the January event is confirmed and safe preparation is established, prioritize coached vault technique and modest approach-speed practice with full recovery. Plyometrics and heavier lifting depend on demonstrated tolerance and are not mandatory. Keep cycling and winter endurance predominantly easy and reduce competing lower-body fatigue. Avoid aggressive weight loss. If the vault event is not pursued, continue enjoyable winter foundation training instead of introducing unnecessary explosive work.

Avoid new exercises, heavy leg loading and fatiguing endurance sessions. Compete only with appropriate technical readiness and symptom control, then take several easy recovery days. If the event is not confirmed, use this as a winter recovery week.

blocks.focus: Return to enjoyable multisport training with two cycling exposures most weeks, two back-tolerant gym sessions and easy skiing, snowshoeing or hiking. Progress run/walk toward a comfortable continuous 30-minute run only if impact is well tolerated. Continue beginner rowing with technique before resistance or duration. Introduce one controlled cycling tempo session weekly when recovered while keeping most endurance time easy. Continue gradual fat loss, monitoring weight trends, appetite and recovery without forcing progress.

blocks.name: Cycling build I: aerobic capacity and durability

Start with tempo or short threshold intervals, then selectively introduce aerobic-power work rather than immediately adding a second hard day. Reassess FTP after consistent training. Maintain strength twice weekly if recovery allows; keep running and rowing optional and easy. Include a lighter final week and practice carbohydrate intake on rides exceeding two hours.

blocks.name: Road transition and 200 km preparation

Progress the long ride toward approximately 4–6 hours only from demonstrated tolerance, combining steady endurance with occasional controlled climbing. Keep one purposeful midweek cycling intensity session and one or two strength sessions with reduced lower-body volume. Test saddle contact, clothing, hand positions, lighting and nutrition. Arrange a professional bike-fit review rather than assuming flexibility alone will resolve blisters or back pain. Practice 60–90 g carbohydrate per hour as tolerated and individualized hydration. Reduce training before the actual April 200 km brevet.

blocks.focus: Complete the April 200 km brevet at a controlled effort and assess pacing, contact-point comfort, fueling and recovery. Schedule several easy days afterward before resuming demanding training. Place a 300 km qualifier here only if its confirmed date and recovery permit; otherwise adjust subsequent blocks. Brevets replace the week's long training ride and usually its demanding interval session. Maintain one gym session and small doses of cycling intensity between events without chasing fatigue.

Introduce back-to-back endurance rides only when useful and recoverable. Retain one short threshold or aerobic-power session in non-event weeks for general cycling fitness. A longer tour race may replace that week's hard endurance session when well separated from a brevet. Maintain strength with low volume and avoid running progression during high cycling loads.

blocks.name: Final qualification and ultra-distance rehearsal

Validate realistic pacing, feeding, saddle management, luggage, visibility and sleep logistics without deliberately practicing unsafe sleep deprivation. Allow substantial recovery afterward, commonly a week or longer before demanding training depending on symptoms. Maintain fitness between events with easy rides and brief quality work rather than additional very long rides. Shift nutrition toward full training support rather than pursuing a weight deadline.

weeks.focus: Repeatable easy cycling, two conservative gym sessions and conditional introductory rowing and run/walk.
weeks.targetLoad: 270 minutes, or 4.5 hours: two 45-minute easy rides, two 45-minute gym sessions including brief rowing technique and mobility, one 70-minute hike/mobility session, one 20-minute run/walk or walk, and one full rest day. weeks.focus: Consolidate back-tolerant strength and easy aerobic consistency with a small conditional duration increase.
weeks.targetLoad: Approximately 4.75–5 hours only if week 2 is completed comfortably and recovery remains normal; otherwise repeat its tolerated load or reduce it. block.rationale: Retain the block's dates and recovery-first purpose. Week 2 targets 4.5 hours, with a clear lower-load option, and week 3 increases only after demonstrated recovery. Maintain one full rest day and at least 48 hours between gym sessions. week.focus: Establish repeatable easy aerobic training and back-tolerant strength, with small rowing and impact-tolerance exposures.

sessions.title: Recovery and readiness check
sessions.description: No formal training. Check sleep, fatigue, leg soreness and back comfort during normal walking and stairs. Establish whether the November 1 hike happened and its duration before increasing training. Confirm the January 7 pole vault event, previous experience and access to qualified coaching; do not introduce jumping or sprinting yet.

sessions.title: Back-tolerant gym and rowing introduction
sessions.description: Allow 45 minutes including rests; proceed only if walking and stairs are comfortable and fatigue is near normal. Warm up with 5 minutes easy stationary cycling, HR below approximately 130 bpm. If pain-free, practice 5 rounds of 1 minute easy rowing and 1 minute standing recovery: light resistance, 18–22 strokes/min, legs-body-arms sequence, comfortable reach and neutral spine. Replace rowing with easy walking if it provokes symptoms. Strength: shallow leg press 1 x 8–10 with pelvis supported; glute bridge 1 x 10–12; lat pulldown 1 x 10 at approximately 30 kg or lighter; machine chest press 1 x 10; Pallof press 1 x 8/side; bird dog 1 x 5/side with 5-second holds. Select loads leaving 4 repetitions in reserve; rest 60–90 seconds. Finish with 5–7 minutes gentle hip-flexor, hamstring and hip-rotation mobility. No loaded hinges, heavy squats or vaulting. Stop for sharp, radiating or increasing back pain and seek assessment.

sessions.title: Steady easy cycling
sessions.description: Ride a flat, familiar route: 10 minutes at 100–120 W, 30 minutes at 120–145 W and 5 minutes easy. Keep conversational effort, RPE 2–3/10, and generally HR below approximately 140 bpm; lower power if effort rises. This maintains cycling-specific aerobic efficiency without interval fatigue. Use lights after work and winter tires as appropriate. On the fatbike, use effort and HR rather than power. Substitute the same trainer session if surfaces are unsafe. If residual weekend fatigue remains, ride 30 minutes total: 10 easy, 15 steady and 5 easy.

sessions.title: Consolidate full-body strength and trunk control
sessions.description: Allow 45 minutes including rests. Warm up with 7 minutes easy stationary cycling, HR below approximately 130 bpm. Use Tuesday's pain-free loads: shallow leg press 1 x 8–10; glute bridge 1 x 10–12; lat pulldown 1 x 10; machine chest press 1 x 10; Pallof press 1 x 8/side; bird dog 1 x 5/side with 5-second holds. Leave 3–4 repetitions in reserve and rest 60–90 seconds. Only if Tuesday and the intervening 48 hours were symptom-free, add a second set to the bridge, pulldown and chest press. Finish with 8–10 minutes gentle hip mobility and relaxed walking. This second exposure reinforces technique and lean-mass retention; do not automatically add squat sets, loaded hinges or explosive work.

sessions.title: Easy cycling without surges
sessions.description: Ride a flat route: 10 minutes at 100–120 W, 30 minutes at 120–150 W and 5 minutes easy. Keep RPE 2–3/10 and generally HR below approximately 140 bpm, without chasing a minimum HR or power. This second cycling exposure reinforces sustainable pedaling and aerobic consistency for later brevet preparation. Avoid hard climbs and spinning-class intensity. Use lights and appropriate tires; substitute the same easy trainer ride if outdoor surfaces are unsafe. Use conversational effort on a bike without a power meter.

sessions.title: Daylight easy hike and hip mobility
sessions.description: Walk or hike for 60 minutes on gentle terrain in daylight, then complete 10 minutes comfortable hip-flexor, hamstring and hip-rotation mobility. Stay conversational at RPE 2–3/10, with provisional HR approximately 110–135 bpm; slow down on climbs. This builds low-impact aerobic time-on-feet and hip movement tolerance without repeating October's large mountain-hike load. Substitute easy snowshoeing only if snow conditions warrant, not as extra training. If recovery is incomplete, reduce to 30 minutes walking plus 10 minutes mobility. Below -15 C, remain within the two-hour outdoor limit.

sessions.title: Conditional beginner run/walk
sessions.description: Proceed only if walking and stairs are comfortable and Saturday caused no back symptoms or residual leg soreness. Walk 5 minutes, complete 5 rounds of 1 minute gentle jogging and 1 minute walking, then walk 5 minutes. Use flat, non-slippery ground in daylight; stay conversational at RPE 2–3/10 with provisional HR below approximately 140–145 bpm. Walk sooner if needed. The purpose is a small, recoverable impact exposure for future running, not extra cardiovascular fatigue. If impact readiness is uncertain but otherwise recovered, walk for 20 minutes instead. Omit entirely if prolonged-weekend fatigue persists; do not make it up. Assess next-morning symptoms before progressing.

week.rationale: Retain the recovery-first structure: Monday rest, two gym sessions separated by 48 hours, two steady cycling exposures, a capped weekend hike and a conditional short run/walk. The full schedule totals 270 minutes, not a mandatory minimum. No records establish what happened October 26–November 1, so do not assume completion or full recovery. If a prolonged November 1 hike or residual fatigue is confirmed, shorten Wednesday to 30 minutes, Saturday to 40 minutes and omit Sunday, giving 205 minutes; reduce further if symptoms warrant. No intervals, heavy hinges, sprints or jumps are needed. No forecast is supplied, so retain outdoor rides in line with the athlete's preference, using lights after work and substituting the trainer for unsafe conditions. Each session develops cycling-specific aerobic maintenance, strength and trunk capacity, low-impact endurance or introductory impact tolerance; none is make-up training. Support slow fat loss with a planned protein-and-fiber afternoon snack, structured meals and approximately 145–180 g protein daily rather than underfueling sessions. Arrange physiotherapy assessment for recurrent back symptoms and confirm qualified vault supervision before sport-specific loading.

season.rationale: The season is anchored on PBP in August 2027, with two intermediate peaks: the pole vault world championship on 7 January 2027 and the April brevet series. Because you can only sustain disciplined training for about 4 months at a time, the plan deliberately alternates focused blocks with maintenance phases rather than one long linear ramp. The first phase rebuilds your detrained base with easy, surge-free aerobic work, back-safe strength, hip mobility, and fat-loss habits — this also builds the posterior-chain strength needed to safely load for vaulting. A short vault-specific block with a taper into 7 January follows, since explosive power and sprint conditioning cannot be developed in the current easy rebuild. After the vault championship we return to the aerobic rebuild through the Norwegian winter, using fatbike, studded-tire riding, cross-country skiing, snowshoeing, and indoor trainer ERG intervals, plus the beginner run and rowing programs. From roughly March, when tarmac riding resumes, we enter a disciplined ~4-month build toward the April 200 km brevet and the rest of the brevet series, with indoor intervals, tempo work, and progressively longer endurance rides. A final specialization block targets PBP-specific demands (back-to-back long rides, night riding, climbing endurance), followed by a short taper. Fat loss proceeds slowly and steadily throughout via dinner and evening-snack control, which also improves your power-to-weight ratio for the hilly brevets and PBP.

week.focus: Re-entry and recovery: stay easy after Sunday's 3h20 hike, complete gym session 2 with Romanian deadlifts, and arrive fresh for the 5-hour hike on 1 November.

sessions.title: Rest day with hip mobility
sessions.description: Full rest after Sunday's 3h20 hike. 15 minutes hip mobility: couch stretch 2x60s/side, 90/90 hip rotations 2x10/side, standing toe-touch progression 2x10, supine hamstring stretch with strap 2x45s/side. Moderate dinner, no evening snacks.

sessions.title: Easy trainer ride, steady 140-150 W
sessions.description: 10 min warm-up at 90-110 W, then 40 min perfectly steady at 140-150 W (ERG mode), cadence 85-95, HR under 145 — back off immediately if it drifts, no surges. 5 min cool-down. Finish with 10 min hip stretching.

sessions.title: Gym session 2: goblet squats + RDL introduction
sessions.description: Warm-up: 5 min easy rowing, HR under 130. Main: goblet squat 3x10 at 12 kg (all three sets today); Romanian deadlift 3x10 with empty bar or 20 kg, strict hip hinge, soft knees, bar close to legs; glute bridge 3x12; lat pulldown 3x10 at 40-45 kg; Pallof press 3x10/side; plank 3x45s. Finish with 12-15 minutes stretching (hip flexors, hamstrings, glutes). Technique first, loads conservative.

sessions.title: Rest day with hip mobility
sessions.description: Full rest to absorb Wednesday's gym session and stay fresh for Sunday's hike. 15 minutes hip mobility as Monday. Watch the evening snacking — this is the key fat-loss habit this week.

sessions.title: Easy trainer ride, steady 140-150 W
sessions.description: 10 min warm-up at 90-110 W, then 40 min steady at 140-150 W in ERG mode, cadence 85-95, flat HR line under 145, zero surges. 5 min cool-down plus 10 min hip stretching. Last stimulus before Sunday's long hike — keep it controlled.

sessions.title: Rest day with short flat walk
sessions.description: Full rest day ahead of the 5-hour hike. Optional 20-30 min flat easy walk if legs feel stiff. 15 min hip mobility, prepare gear and food for tomorrow's hike. Early dinner, no evening snacks.

sessions.title: 5-hour endurance hike
sessions.description: Long mountain hike, ~5 hours moving, 800-1000 m elevation. Keep HR under 135 on the flat and under 145 even on steep pitches — walk steep sections with short strides rather than surging. Summit and food stops under 5 minutes each. Carry plenty of food and drink; eat 40-60 g carbs per hour. This anchors the week's aerobic volume.

week.rationale: Sunday's mountain hike was far more than the planned light close, so this week stays genuinely easy to absorb it and be fresh for the 5-hour hike on 1 November. Only two short steady trainer rides and one gym session serve as training stimuli; rest days and hip mobility fill the rest. The gym session adds the third goblet squat set at 12 kg and introduces light Romanian deadlifts with a strict hip hinge — the posterior-chain foundation needed for vault loading in December — plus 12-15 minutes of stretching to actually move the needle on those hips. Trainer rides target 140-150 W with a flat HR line under 145. Fat-loss focus stays on dinner portion control and avoiding evening snacks, especially important this week since activity is low.

today.title: Rest day with hip mobility
today.description: Full rest after Sunday's 3h20 mountain hike. Do 15 minutes of hip mobility: couch stretch 2x60s/side, 90/90 hip rotations 2x10/side, standing toe-touch progression (bent-knee to straight-knee) 2x10, supine hamstring stretch with strap 2x45s/side. Keep dinner moderate and skip evening snacks.
alternatives: If you feel restless, a 20-minute flat easy walk is fine, but no cycling or strength work today.
today.rationale: Yesterday's hike was roughly four times the planned volume with HR sustained in the 140s–160s, so the 'light close' to the re-entry week didn't happen. Full rest today is the best way to absorb that load and arrive fresh for the 5-hour hike on 1 November. The hip mobility directly targets the flexibility limiting your riding position and sit-bone comfort on long rides.
today.optionalRationale: The hip mobility work is the one stimulus that costs little energy yet directly builds the hip flexibility you need for a more aerodynamic, sit-bone-friendly position on the April brevet and PBP. Skipping it delays the flexibility adaptation that strength training alone won't provide.

tomorrow.title: Easy trainer ride, steady 140-150 W
tomorrow.description: 10 min warm-up at 90-110 W, then 40 min perfectly steady at 140-150 W in ERG mode, cadence 85-95, HR must stay under 145 — if it drifts above, back off immediately, no surges. 5 min cool-down. Finish with 10 minutes of hip stretching.
alternatives: If the trainer is unavailable, an easy 60-minute fatbike ride at conversational effort, HR under 145.
tomorrow.rationale: A short, surge-free aerobic stimulus that re-establishes the steady-effort pattern we're rebuilding after the erratic 15 October spinning classes, without adding meaningful fatigue before Sunday's 5-hour hike.
tomorrow.optionalRationale: This session rebuilds the aerobic base and flat-effort discipline that carries you through the April 200 km brevet and PBP — the exact pattern that failed (surge-recover) on 15 October. Skipping it loses one of only two aerobic stimuli this week, slowing the rebuild of your detrained base toward the 220 W-plus fitness needed before the winter block.

sessions.description: 60 min indoor ERG ride: 10 min warm-up at 90-110 W, 40 min steady at 140-155 W (HR 125-145, cadence 85-95), 10 min cool-down. Flat effort line, no surges.

sessions.title: Easy walk
sessions.description: 45-60 min flat easy walk, HR under 120. Optional 10 minutes of hip mobility afterward.

sessions.title: Easy trainer ride

sessions.title: Run/walk session
sessions.description: 30 min run/walk if legs feel fresh: 4 min easy jog / 1 min walk, HR under 145 throughout. If legs are heavy, replace with a 45 min brisk walk. Follow with 10 min stretching.

sessions.title: Easy hike or walk
sessions.description: 60-90 min easy hike or flat walk, HR under 135 on climbs — short strides on steep pitches, stops under 5 minutes. Genuinely easy; the volume ramp starts next week.

week.rationale: Sunday's 5-hour hike was your biggest session since July, so this week stays deliberately light: two short steady trainer rides, one gym session progressing the back-safe strength work, the resumed run/walk, and easy walks. All cycling stays flat-effort at 140-155 W with HR under 145, no spinning classes, and stretching is extended to 10-15 minutes to actually move the needle on your hip mobility. This recovery week is what allows the volume ramp in week 3 without setbacks.

today.title: Rest and hip mobility
today.description: Full rest after Sunday's 5-hour hike — the biggest session since your July bikepacking race. Do 10-15 minutes of hip mobility: couch stretch, 90/90 hip rotations, hamstring flossing, and standing forward-fold progressions (knees soft, working toward a straight-leg toe touch over the coming weeks).
alternatives: If you feel restless, a 20-30 minute flat walk is fine, but nothing more.
today.rationale: Sunday's hike was a large aerobic and eccentric load for your current detrained state, and last week's hike (25 October) already left some residual fatigue. A genuine rest day today is what lets the adaptation happen and protects your back and hips before Tuesday's ride and Wednesday's gym session.
today.optionalRationale: Rest is the best choice today: skipping this recovery day would compromise absorption of Sunday's effort and risk back or hip issues, so there is no optionality to assess.

tomorrow.title: Easy trainer ride
tomorrow.description: 60 min indoor ERG ride: 10 min warm-up at 90-110 W, 40 min steady at 140-155 W (HR 125-145, cadence 85-95), 10 min cool-down at 90-110 W. Keep the power and HR lines flat — no surges, no spinning-class patterns.
alternatives: If legs are still heavy from the hike, do 45 min at 120-140 W instead.
If you prefer dry outdoor riding, a 60 min flat fatbike or gravel ride at the same easy effort works.
tomorrow.rationale: This is the first easy aerobic stimulus after the hike, deliberately short and flat to re-engage the aerobic system while you absorb Sunday's effort. Steady ERG work at 140-155 W directly rebuilds the aerobic base you'll need for the April 200 km brevet and PBP, and the flat-effort discipline corrects the surge-recover pattern from the 15 October spinning classes.
tomorrow.optionalRationale: Skipping it costs a day of rebuilding the steady aerobic engine that everything from the brevet series to PBP sits on — and breaks the habit consistency this whole foundation block is about.
